definition_zh: 微不足道的；少得可怜的；可鄙的
definition_en: so small or mean that it invites contempt rather than respect
core_image: 桌上只有一小碟，里面三粒豆子，主人却说这是全部家当
scene: 他干了一整月，拿到的钱还不够付一半房租。 He worked the whole month and was paid a sum that would not cover half the rent, a paltry reward for so much time.
sceneCN: 这里 paltry 指报酬菲薄（第 6 个义项：报酬菲薄）；句意为他干了一整月，报酬少得连一半房租都不够。

pos.zh: 微不足道的；少得可怜的；可鄙的

senses.title: Insignificantly small
senses.definition: of a quantity, below what the situation plainly deserves
senses.definitionCN: 数量低于情形明显应得的水平
senses.example: Three beans on a plate would be a paltry meal.
senses.exampleCN: 盘里三粒豆子，是少得可怜的一餐。
senses.why: The word measures by expectation: smallness alone is not enough.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按期待衡量：单是「小」还不足以构成它。

senses.title: A contemptible amount
senses.definition: of money, so little that it reads as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 钱少到读起来像侮辱
senses.example: They offered a paltry compensation and called it fair.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给出一笔微薄补偿，还称之为公平。
senses.why: Money is the word's most common home because prices can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 钱是这个词最常见的住处，因为价码可以比较。

senses.title: A feeble excuse
senses.definition: of an explanation, thin enough to show it was not meant
senses.definitionCN: 解释薄到一看就知道不是真话
senses.example: He gave a paltry excuse about the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿交通作了个拙劣借口。
senses.why: The word judges the effort behind the words, not their length.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判话语背后的用心，而不是话语的长短。

senses.title: A token effort
senses.definition: of work, done just enough to be visible and no more
senses.definitionCN: 干活只干到能被看见的程度，一点不多
senses.example: The clean-up was a paltry effort and the street stayed dirty.
senses.exampleCN: 清扫只是敷衍了事，街道依旧脏。
senses.why: Here smallness is a choice, which makes it contemptible.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「小」是一种选择，因此可鄙。

senses.title: A sum that shames
senses.definition: of a payment, low enough to embarrass the payer and the paid
senses.definitionCN: 款项低到让付款者和收款者都难堪
senses.example: The prize was a paltry fifty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金只有寒酸的五十镑。
senses.why: The word often carries the speaker's flush of shame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带着说话者脸上一热的那种难堪。

senses.title: Meagre reward
senses.definition: of a return for labour, far below the time it took
senses.definitionCN: 劳动所得远低于所花的时间
senses.example: He worked the month for a paltry reward.
senses.exampleCN: 他干了一个月，报酬菲薄。
senses.why: Fairness enters here: the sum is judged against the hours.
senses.whyCN: 公平在这里进场：款子是跟小时数比的。

senses.title: A petty reason
senses.definition: of a motive, small in a way that lowers the person who holds it
senses.definitionCN: 动机小得让持有它的人显得低下
senses.example: Jealousy is a paltry reason to ruin a friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 因嫉妒毁掉友谊，是卑琐的理由。
senses.why: The word can turn from the thing to the mind that wants it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从物转向想要它的那颗心。

senses.title: Beneath notice
senses.definition: of a thing, not worth the attention it asks for
senses.definitionCN: 不值得它所索取的注意
senses.example: The objection was paltry and the meeting moved on.
senses.exampleCN: 那点异议不值一提，会议继续往下走。
senses.why: Used this way the word dismisses rather than measures.
senses.whyCN: 这样用时，这个词是在驱散，而不是在衡量。

intro.en: Paltry is a word of uncertain origin, probably built from an old word for a rag or a scrap.
intro.cn: paltry 来源不确定，很可能由某个意为「破布、碎屑」的古词构成。

items.en: An English dialect word palt or pelt meant 'a rag, a worthless scrap'.
items.cn: 英语方言词 palt 或 pelt 意为「破布、没用的碎屑」。

items.en: The ending -ry made nouns of quality or collection, as in rivalry and jewellery.
items.cn: 词尾 -ry 构成表性质或集合的名词，如 rivalry 与 jewellery。

items.en: Paltry appears in sixteenth-century writing, already meaning 'worthless, contemptible'.
items.cn: paltry 见于十六世纪文字，当时已意为「无价值的、可鄙的」。

items.en: The nineteenth century fixed it to small sums of money and small wages.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它固定用于小额钱款与菲薄工资。

items.en: Today it judges excuses and efforts as readily as amounts.
items.cn: 今天它评判借口与作为，和评判数额一样顺手。

note.en: The look-alike group is the paltry family; the near-meaning group separates trifling, meagre, piddling and negligible.
note.cn: 形近组是 paltry 词族；近义组把「琐碎」「微薄」「小气」与「可忽略」分开。

entries.definition: more worthless by comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 相比之下更不值钱的。

entries.definition: most worthless of all.
entries.definitionCN: 最不值一提的。

entries.definition: the quality of being paltry.
entries.definitionCN: 微薄可鄙的性质。

entries.definition: skins or furs as goods.
entries.definitionCN: 毛皮货。

entries.definition: too small to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 小到不必在意的。

entries.definition: thin and insufficient.
entries.definitionCN: 单薄不足的。

entries.definition: annoyingly small.
entries.definitionCN: 小得令人不快的。

entries.definition: small enough to ignore.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以忽略的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of three beans offered as a whole meal.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「三粒豆子被当作一顿饭」的画面。

normal.en: Paltry sounds like 'poultry' scraps: the bits nobody would buy.
normal.cn: paltry 听起来像 poultry（家禽）的碎屑：没人肯买的边角。

normal.en: Think of a plate with three beans and a proud host.
normal.cn: 想象一只盘子三粒豆子，主人还很得意。

normal.en: Pal-try: try with a 'pal', and even a friend would not call this enough.
normal.cn: pal-try：和 pal（朋友）一起 try，连朋友都不会说这够了。

normal.en: Say PAWL-tree; the long first syllable makes the thing sound emptier.
normal.cn: 读成 PAWL-tree，第一个音节拖长，东西听起来更空。

normal.en: Pair it with sum: a paltry sum is one that apologises for itself.
normal.cn: 把它和 sum 配对：paltry sum 是一笔自带歉意的款子。

abstract.en: Paltry is a comparison wearing the clothes of a description.
abstract.cn: paltry 是穿了描述外衣的比较。

abstract.en: The word is most damaging when applied to effort, because effort could have been more.
abstract.cn: 这个词用在「作为」上最伤人，因为作为本可以更多。

abstract.en: Small is neutral; paltry is small with a verdict attached.
abstract.cn: 小是中性的；paltry 是带着判决的小。

examples.en: He worked the whole month for a paltry reward.
examples.cn: 他干了一整月，报酬菲薄。

examples.en: They offered a paltry compensation and called it fair.
examples.cn: 他们给出一笔微薄补偿，还称之为公平。

examples.en: Jealousy is a paltry reason to ruin a friendship.
examples.cn: 因嫉妒毁掉友谊，是卑琐的理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: palt（古词「破布、碎屑」）+ ry（名词尾）：只值一块破布的东西，就是「微不足道的」。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为出自方言词 palt／pelt（破布、碎屑）加后缀 -ry

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all shrink something and then judge it: a meal, a sum, an excuse, an effort, a prize, a wage, a motive and an objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都先把某物缩小，再作评判：一餐、一笔钱、一个借口、一番作为、一份奖、一份工资、一个动机与一点异议。

core.en: THREE BEANS CALLED A MEAL
core.cn: 三粒豆子被称作一餐

branches.en: A small quantity and a small sum of money.
branches.cn: 少量的东西与微薄的款子。

branches.en: A thin excuse and an effort that stops at being seen.
branches.cn: 单薄的借口与只做到被看见的作为。

branches.en: A prize that shames and a wage that does not meet the hours.
branches.cn: 令人难堪的奖与不抵工时的工资。

branches.en: A motive small enough to lower its holder.
branches.cn: 小到让持有者显得低下的动机。

branches.en: A thing dismissed rather than measured.
branches.cn: 被驱散而不是被衡量的东西。

intro.en: The paltry family is thin: the adjective, its comparison and its noun, all built on the same scrap.
intro.cn: paltry 词族很单薄：形容词、比较级与名词，全都长在同一块碎屑上。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin source; the entries below are the neighbouring vocabulary of smallness and worthlessness.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源；下面这些条目是「小」与「无价值」的邻近词汇。

items.exampleCN: 接着来了一个更寒酸的提议。

definition_zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少；资源不足以满足需求的状态
definition_en: the state in which something needed exists in a quantity too small to satisfy the demand for it
core_image: 集市收摊时只剩最后一筐苹果，围上来的人却比开市时更多
scene: 集市收摊后，最后一筐苹果前反而围了更多人，摊主悄悄翻过价格牌。 Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
sceneCN: 这里 scarcity 指「物品稀少而需求仍在，因而产生溢价的情形」（第 9 个义项：因稀少而形成的附加价值）；句意为稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。图中可辨识物件：空摊位、最后一筐苹果、围拢的人群、翻面的价牌。

pos.zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少（可数指具体的一次短缺，不可数指普遍状态）

senses.title: A shortage of something needed
senses.definition: the condition in which the supply of a needed thing is smaller than the amount people require
senses.definitionCN: 所需之物的供给小于人们所需数量的状况
senses.example: Scarcity of clean water shaped the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净水的短缺塑造了这座小镇的历史。
senses.why: Scarcity names a relationship, not a count: the same amount can be plentiful in one place and scarce in another because demand differs.
senses.whyCN: scarcity 命名的是关系而非数量：同样的量在一处充裕、在另一处稀缺，因为需求不同。

senses.title: Limited means against unlimited wants
senses.titleCN: 经济学：有限资源面对无限欲望
senses.definition: the founding condition of economics, in which resources are finite while human wants are not
senses.definitionCN: 经济学的出发点：资源有限而人的欲望无限
senses.example: Economics begins with scarcity and asks how to allocate.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学从稀缺出发，追问如何分配。
senses.why: Political economy took the everyday word and made it the reason markets and choices exist at all.
senses.whyCN: 政治经济学把这个日常词提升为市场与选择之所以存在的理由。

senses.title: The rarity of a particular object
senses.definition: the quality of being hard to find or obtain, as of a rare book or a scarce stamp
senses.definitionCN: 难以找到或取得的性质，如稀见书或罕邮票
senses.example: The scarcity of the first edition made it expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 初版书的稀有使它昂贵。
senses.why: Collectors use the word for the object itself, because what matters is how few survive rather than how many are wanted.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者用这个词指物本身，因为要紧的是存世多少，而不是多少人想要。

senses.title: Resource depletion in ecology
senses.definition: the falling availability of a natural resource as it is used up or its habitat shrinks
senses.definitionCN: 自然资源因被耗尽或栖息地缩小而日益不可得
senses.example: Scarcity of nesting sites reduced the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 营巢地的稀缺使这个群落变小。
senses.why: Ecology views scarcity as a limit that shapes behaviour, competition and population size.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把稀缺看作塑造行为、竞争与种群规模的限制。

senses.title: Perceived scarcity and the mindset it creates
senses.titleCN: 感知到的稀缺及其心态
senses.definition: a felt shortage that narrows attention, encourages hoarding and pushes people toward short-term choices
senses.definitionCN: 感到的短缺，它会收窄注意力、促使人囤积并偏向短期选择
senses.example: A scarcity mindset kept the team from sharing information.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺心态让这个团队不愿共享信息。
senses.why: Psychology separated the state from the perception, because people act on what they believe is scarce.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把状态与感知分开，因为人是按自己所相信的稀缺去行动的。

senses.title: Not enough hours in the day
senses.definition: the shortage of time relative to the tasks and commitments one has accepted
senses.definitionCN: 相对于已接受的任务与承诺而言的时间不足
senses.example: Time scarcity, not money, kept her from finishing the course.
senses.exampleCN: 让她没能修完课程的，是时间稀缺而非缺钱。
senses.why: The word extends easily to time, because hours are a fixed supply that cannot be increased by effort.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很容易延伸到时上，因为小时是固定供给，再努力也加不出来。

senses.title: Attention and information scarcity
senses.definition: the shortage of attention available for a flood of information, or of reliable information itself
senses.definitionCN: 面对信息洪流时注意力的不足，或可靠信息本身的不足
senses.example: Information scarcity was replaced by information overload.
senses.exampleCN: 信息稀缺已被信息过载取代。
senses.why: Media economics applied the word to attention, since the scarce thing in an abundant market is the audience's focus.
senses.whyCN: 传媒经济学把这个词用到注意力上，因为在充裕的市场里，稀缺的是受众的专注。

senses.title: Artificial scarcity created on purpose
senses.titleCN: 为获利而人为制造的稀缺
senses.definition: a shortage deliberately maintained by a seller, cartel or platform to keep prices or status high
senses.definitionCN: 卖方、卡特尔或平台为维持高价或地位而有意保持的短缺
senses.example: The limited release was artificial scarcity, not a real shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 限量发售是人为稀缺，并非真的缺货。
senses.why: Once scarcity can be manufactured, the word no longer assumes a natural limit; it can describe a strategy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦稀缺可以被制造，这个词就不再假定自然极限，而可以指一种策略。

senses.title: The premium that rarity adds to value
senses.titleCN: 因稀少而产生的价值溢价
senses.definition: the extra price or prestige an item gains because few like it are available
senses.definitionCN: 物品因同类稀少而获得的额外价格或声望
senses.example: Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。
senses.why: Value can come from the supply side alone: when the same thing is abundant it is cheap, and when it is nearly gone it is dear.
senses.whyCN: 价值可以只来自供给一侧：同样的东西多时便宜，快没有时就贵。

intro.en: Scarcity came into English from Old French in the fourteenth century, but its deeper root is disputed between two accounts that are still taught side by side. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: scarcity 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，但其更深词源在两种说法之间至今仍有争议，两种说法常并列讲授。年代均为约数。

items.en: One account derives scarcitas from parcus 'sparing, frugal'. The deeper origin of parcus is uncertain; the suggestion that it comes from parcere 'to spare' is a hypothesis rather than a proved link.
items.cn: 一种说法把 scarcitas 追溯到 parcus「节省的、俭省的」。parcus 的更深来源不确定；认为它出自 parcere「节省」的说法是假说，而非已证实的联系。

items.en: Scarcitas meant 'scarcity, scantiness'. On this account the noun passed into Old French as scarcete and then into English.
items.cn: scarcitas 意为「短缺、稀少」。按这一说法，该名词进入古法语作 scarcete，再进入英语。

items.en: Old French scarcete meant 'smallness, scantiness, stinginess' and English scarcity first carried that sense of meagre supply before widening to any shortage.
items.cn: 古法语 scarcete 意为「少、不足、吝啬」，英语 scarcity 最初带这种「供给寒酸」的意思，后扩为任何短缺。

items.en: The competing account connects the adjective scarce to Vulgar Latin excarpsus 'plucked out', from ex- 'out' plus carpere 'to pluck'. This account explains the adjective but does not settle the noun.
items.cn: 对立说法把形容词 scarce 连到俗拉丁 excarpsus「被摘出的」，出自 ex-「向外」加 carpere「摘取」。这一说法解释了形容词，却未能定下名词的来源。

items.en: From the nineteenth century classical economics made scarcity the central condition of economic life, and the word acquired its technical sense of finite means against unlimited wants.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，古典经济学把稀缺定为经济生活的核心条件，这个词于是获得「有限手段面对无限欲望」的技术义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the derivation is disputed between parcus and excarpsus, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the modern economic sense, so its first date is approximate; any older Indo-European forms offered for this family are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：词源在 parcus 与 excarpsus 之间存疑，现代经济义也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；凡为这个词族给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to scarcity but differ in part of speech, meaning or root; group two holds other nouns of not having enough, each with a different reason for the shortfall.
note.cn: 第一组是与 scarcity 形近、但词性、含义或词根不同的词；第二组是其他表示「不够」的名词，每一个的短缺原因都不同。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'hard to obtain in quantity'; scarcity is the noun built on it in meaning, even where the derivation is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「数量稀少、难以取得」；scarcity 在语义上是它的名词形式，尽管词源仍有争议。

entries.definition: Means 'barely, hardly', not 'sparsely'; the adverb has drifted away from the idea of quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「几乎不、勉强」，而非「稀少地」；这个副词已偏离数量概念。

entries.definition: Thinly spread, from Latin sparsus 'scattered'; it looks close to scarce but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 分布稀疏的，出自拉丁 sparsus「散开的」；与 scarce 外形相近，但并无共同词根。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym of scarcity formed with -ness; it names the state without the economic overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的较罕用同义词；它只指状态，不带经济学色彩。

entries.definition: A plain word for a supply that is below the amount required, usually temporary or local.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给低于所需数量的普通词，通常是临时或局部的。

entries.definition: An old word for a scarce supply, especially of food; it comes from dear in the sense of costly, not from scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给稀少、尤指食物的旧词；它出自表示「昂贵」的 dear，而非出自 scarcity。

entries.definition: A formal noun for a small number or amount, from Latin paucus 'few'; it stresses fewness rather than unmet demand.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指数量很少，出自拉丁 paucus「少」；它强调数量少，而非需求未被满足。

entries.definition: The quality of being uncommon; a rare thing may be plentiful in absolute terms and still be uncommon in kind.
entries.definitionCN: 不常见的性质；稀见之物在绝对数量上可能很多，只是在种类上少见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun of scarce; the -ity ending turns the adjective into a state.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词，-ity 后缀把形容词变成状态。

normal.en: The economic sense is fixed in one phrase: limited resources against unlimited wants.
normal.cn: 经济义固定在一句话里：有限资源面对无限欲望。

normal.en: The family runs scarce, scarcely, scarceness, scarcity and water-scarce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 scarce、scarcely、scarceness、scarcity 与 water-scarce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: water scarcity, food scarcity, resource scarcity, artificial scarcity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：水资源短缺、粮食短缺、资源稀缺、人为稀缺。

normal.en: Sparse looks like scarce but comes from sparsus 'scattered', so the two are false relatives.
normal.cn: sparse 看起来像 scarce，却出自 sparsus「散开的」，两者是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture the last basket on a table and every hand reaching at once.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上最后一筐，所有手同时伸过去。

abstract.en: Picture a day with more tasks than hours, so each choice costs another choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一天里任务多过小时，每个选择都要用另一个选择来换。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf kept almost empty on purpose so that the few items look precious.
abstract.cn: 想象货架故意留得几乎空着，好让剩下的几件显得珍贵。

examples.en: Classical economics treats scarcity as the reason choice is necessary.
examples.cn: 古典经济学把稀缺视为选择之所以必要的原因。

examples.en: The scarcity of rare earths reshaped the electronics supply chain.
examples.cn: 稀土资源的稀缺重塑了电子产业供应链。

examples.en: Artificial scarcity can keep a price high long after demand has fallen.
examples.cn: 人为稀缺可以在需求下降很久之后仍把价格维持在高位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「scarce（稀少）+ ity」——东西少、要的人多 → 稀缺、短缺

root: 古法语 scarcete < 拉丁 scarcitas「短缺」；词根一说为 parcus「俭省的」，另一说与俗拉丁 excarpsus「摘出的」（ex- + carpere）相关，两说并存未定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one relation: a supply is smaller than the demand on it. The word then becomes the foundation of economics, the state of a rare object, an ecological limit, a mindset, a shortage of time, of attention, a shortage made on purpose and finally a premium on price.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个关系展开：供给小于对它的需求。这个词随后成为经济学的基础、稀见物的状态、生态的限制、一种心态、时间与注意力的不足、有意制造的不足，最后是价格上的溢价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one last basket on an emptying table while more hands reach for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：空下去的桌上只剩最后一筐，伸过来的手却更多。

branches.en: THE GAP: the everyday shortfall and the founding condition of economics are the same relation formalised.
branches.cn: 缺口：日常的不足与经济学的出发点，是同一关系被形式化。

branches.en: FEWNESS: a rare object and a depleted habitat are both cases of supply falling.
branches.cn: 稀少：稀见之物与枯竭的栖息地，都是供给下降的情形。

branches.en: MIND: perception can produce the behaviour of scarcity before the shortage arrives.
branches.cn: 心态：感知可以在短缺到来之前就制造出稀缺的行为。

branches.en: NON-MATERIAL: hours and attention are fixed or finite supplies of their own.
branches.cn: 非实物：小时与注意力本身就是固定或有限的供给。

branches.en: MADE AND PRICED: scarcity can be staged, and rarity can be charged for.
branches.cn: 制造与定价：稀缺可以被安排出来，稀少也可以被收费。

intro.en: Scarcity is a noun formed with a Latin state suffix on a stem whose own origin is disputed, so the suffix is certain while the root is not.
intro.cn: scarcity 是用拉丁状态后缀构成的名称，词干本身的来源有争议，因此后缀确定而词根不确定。

latinIntro.en: The state suffix -itas gives English -ity in scarcity, rarity and paucity; the root is variously traced to parcus 'sparing' or to excarpsus 'plucked out'.
latinIntro.cn: 状态后缀 -itas 在 scarcity、rarity 与 paucity 中作英语 -ity；词根则有 parcus「俭省的」与 excarpsus「摘出的」两种追溯。

definition_zh: 分层；层叠；层理；层层叠加的手法或效果
definition_en: the act or result of arranging something in layers, or the effect of several layers seen together
core_image: 陶罐剖面露出三道不同颜色的泥条，像被压在一起的三张薄纸
scene: 陶罐剖面显示三道不同颜色的泥条，制陶人说明那是分次盘筑留下的痕迹。 Careful layering of clay gave the jar walls their even thickness.
sceneCN: 这里 layering 指「把材料一层层叠加的做法」（第 1 个义项：把材料分成层来堆叠的动作）；句意为细心的泥料分层使罐壁厚度均匀。图中可辨识物件：陶罐剖面、三道泥条、制陶人的手、刮刀。

pos.zh: 分层；层叠；层理；（艺术、设计中的）层次叠加
layer 的现在分词：把……分层放置；层层叠加

senses.title: Putting material down in layers
senses.titleCN: 把材料一层层叠加的做法
senses.definition: the act of building something up by adding one layer of material after another
senses.definitionCN: 通过一次次添加一层材料把某物堆叠起来
senses.example: Careful layering of clay gave the jar walls their even thickness.
senses.exampleCN: 细心的泥料分层使罐壁厚度均匀。
senses.why: layer plus -ing names the activity, so the emphasis is on the sequence of additions rather than on the finished stack.
senses.whyCN: layer 加 -ing 命名这一活动，重点在一次次添加的次序，而非完成的叠层。

senses.title: Bedding in rock or sediment
senses.definition: the formation of distinct beds as sediment settles out in successive episodes
senses.definitionCN: 沉积物在一次次事件中落下而形成独立层的过程
senses.example: Fine layering in the silt marks each quiet season of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 粉砂中细密的层理标出湖的每一个平静季节。
senses.why: geology uses the word for the process behind bedding, which is why it often appears beside stratification.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个词指层理背后的过程，因此它常与 stratification 一同出现。

senses.title: Depth built by overlapping shapes
senses.titleCN: 绘画与设计中用重叠形制造纵深
senses.definition: the technique of overlapping shapes, colours or transparencies so that the eye reads depth
senses.definitionCN: 通过重叠形状、颜色或透明层，使眼睛读出纵深的手法
senses.example: The illustrator built depth by layering translucent washes.
senses.exampleCN: 插画师用层层透明淡彩造出纵深。
senses.why: art borrowed the physical verb: each wash lies over the last, so depth is literally an accumulation of sheets.
senses.whyCN: 艺术借用了这个实义动词：每层淡彩压在前一层上，纵深就是薄片的实际累积。

senses.title: Wearing clothes in layers
senses.definition: the practice of wearing several garments one over another for warmth or style
senses.definitionCN: 为保暖或造型而把数件衣物套穿在一起
senses.example: Layering is the only way to stay warm on a wet ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 在湿冷山脊上，多层穿衣是唯一保暖的办法。
senses.why: outdoor writing treats the noun as a technique, and the layers can be added or removed as conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 户外写作把这个名词当作一种方法，各层可随环境增减。

senses.title: Stacking sounds in a mix
senses.definition: the technique of combining several recordings or parts so that they sound as one richer texture
senses.definitionCN: 把多条录音或声部合成一个更厚实整体的技术
senses.example: The producer got that warmth from layering three takes of the same chord.
senses.exampleCN: 制作人把同一和弦的三次录音叠加，得到那种温暖感。
senses.why: studio usage extends the verb to sound, which also stacks: each take is a sheet laid over the mix.
senses.whyCN: 录音室用法把这个动词扩展到声音，声音同样叠压：每条录音都是铺在混音上的一层。

senses.title: Levels in a system design
senses.definition: the arrangement of a system into levels, each with its own job and a narrow interface to the next
senses.definitionCN: 把系统分成若干层，每层职责独立并与相邻层以窄接口相连
senses.example: Layering lets you replace the storage level without touching the display code.
senses.exampleCN: 分层使你可以更换存储层而不碰显示代码。
senses.why: software borrowed the noun because layered designs can be changed one sheet at a time.
senses.whyCN: 软件借用这个名词，因为分层设计可以一次只改一层。

senses.title: Ranked levels in an organization
senses.definition: the division of an organization or society into levels of authority or status
senses.definitionCN: 组织或社会按权力或地位分成层级
senses.example: Too much layering slowed every decision to a crawl.
senses.exampleCN: 层级过多使每个决定都慢得像爬。
senses.why: the metaphor is critical here: layering is often named as the problem rather than the solution.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比喻带批评意味：分层常被指为问题而非解法。

senses.title: Levels of meaning or memory
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：意义或记忆的层层叠加
senses.definition: the presence of several levels of meaning, memory or interpretation within one thing
senses.definitionCN: 同一事物内部存在若干层意义、记忆或解读
senses.example: The novel rewards layering: each rereading adds a stratum the first reading missed.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说值得层层读：每次重读都添上初读错过的一层。
senses.why: abstract usage makes the noun analytical, naming what a reader or listener must peel apart.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法使这个名词具分析性，指读者或听者必须逐层剥开的东西。

intro.en: Layering is lay plus -er plus -ing. Lay descends from Old English lecgan 'to place', the causative of lie, and layer was first 'one who lays' before it meant a sheet. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: layering 由 lay 加 -er 再加 -ing 构成。lay 源自古英语 lecgan「放置」，是 lie 的使役形式；layer 最初指「放置者」，后才指一层。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lecgan meant 'to place, put down', and it was the causative partner of licgan 'to lie'; the pair survives as lay and lie.
items.cn: lecgan 意为「放置、放下」，是 licgan「躺」的使役配对；这一对至今保留为 lay 与 lie。

items.en: The agent suffix -er first made layer mean 'one who lays', as in a layer of bricks, a bricklayer.
items.cn: -er 这个施事后缀最初使 layer 指「放置者」，如砌砖的人。

items.en: In the seventeenth century layer shifted from the person to the thing laid, and so came to mean a stratum or coating.
items.cn: 十七世纪 layer 从人转指被放置之物，于是意为层或涂层。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries added -ing to name the activity, first in craft and geology, then in art and technology.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪加 -ing 命名这一活动，先用于手艺与地质，后用于艺术与技术。

items.en: Sound mixing, software design and social criticism each took the word for their own stacked levels.
items.cn: 声音混制、软件设计与社会批评各自借这个词指自己的叠层。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Old English verb is well attested, but its pre-Germanic ancestry is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：古英语动词有充分书证，但其日耳曼语之前的谱系属重构而非有记录。

note.en: Group one sorts layering from words that look close but are built differently; group two sorts it from near words for layers and levels.
note.cn: 第一组把 layering 与形近但构词不同的词分开；第二组区分它与「层」「级」的近似说法。

entries.definition: The layer itself or the verb; layering names the activity or the combined effect of several layers.
entries.definitionCN: 指层本身或动词；layering 指这一活动或若干层的合成效果。

entries.definition: The gerund of lay alone: placing something down once, without the sense of repeated sheets.
entries.definitionCN: 只是 lay 的动名词：放下一次，不含反复叠层之意。

entries.definition: From Old English leger 'a place to lie', related to lie but not to lay; it means an animal's den.
entries.definitionCN: 源自古英语 leger「躺卧之处」，与 lie 相关而与 lay 无关；指兽穴。

entries.definition: Ends in -yer, a different spelling of the agent suffix, and has nothing to do with placing.
entries.definitionCN: 以 -yer 结尾，是施事后缀的另一种拼法，与放置无关。

entries.definition: The geological and sociological term for layer formation; layering is its plainer counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 地质与社会学中表示成层的术语；layering 是其更朴素的对应词。

entries.definition: Putting whole objects one on another, as boxes; layering usually means thin sheets of material.
entries.definitionCN: 把整件物体一个个叠起，如箱子；layering 通常指材料的薄层。

entries.definition: A single covering applied to a surface; layering implies several such coverings in sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 施加在表面上的一层覆盖物；layering 意味着若干层依次叠加。

entries.definition: A system of ranks with authority; layering describes the physical or conceptual act of stacking levels.
entries.definitionCN: 带权力的等级体系；layering 描述把层级叠起的实体或概念动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: lay + -er + -ing: the act of putting sheet after sheet in place.
normal.cn: lay + -er + -ing：把一层层薄片放上去的动作。

normal.en: The family runs layer, layered, layering, multilayer, delayer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 layer、layered、layering、multilayer、delayer。

normal.en: Craft, geology, art, sound and software all use the same image of stacked sheets.
normal.cn: 手艺、地质、艺术、声音与软件都用同一张叠层意象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: layering of clay, sound layering, layering effect.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：泥料分层、声音叠加、层次效果。

normal.en: Compare lay and lie: you lay a sheet down, but the sheet lies on the table.
normal.cn: 比较 lay 与 lie：你把薄片放下，薄片躺在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture three translucent sheets of coloured paper held up to a window.
abstract.cn: 想象三张半透明彩纸对着窗举起。

abstract.en: Picture an onion cut in half, every ring a season.
abstract.cn: 想象洋葱被切成两半，每一圈是一季。

abstract.en: Picture a joke that also works as an accusation if you hear the lower layer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑话，若听出下面那层，同时是一句指责。

examples.en: The potter's layering produced a wall that dried without cracking.
examples.cn: 陶工的分层做法使罐壁干燥而不开裂。

examples.en: Layering three instruments gave the theme an unexpected weight.
examples.cn: 叠加三件乐器使主题有了意外的分量。

examples.en: Good layering in a drawing keeps the eye moving between depths.
examples.cn: 绘画中良好的层次让目光在纵深间移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「layer（层）+ ing（动作）」——一层层往上放 → 分层、叠层

root: 古英语 lecgan「放置」（lie 的使役形式）+ 施事后缀 -er + 动名词后缀 -ing；layer 十七世纪由「放置者」转指「层」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one action, the placing of a sheet over a sheet, then spread from clay to rock, paint, clothes, sound, software, ranks and meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：把一层盖在另一层上，随后从泥料扩展到岩石、绘画、衣着、声音、软件、等级与意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet laid over another until depth appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层压一层，直到纵深出现。

branches.en: PHYSICAL ADDING: clay and clothing are both built one sheet at a time.
branches.cn: 实体添加：泥料与衣着都是一层一层加出来的。

branches.en: BEDDING: sediment repeats the gesture until rock is banded.
branches.cn: 层理：沉积重复同一动作，直到岩石成带。

branches.en: DEPTH OF SENSATION: paint washes and sound takes overlap to build a fuller surface.
branches.cn: 感官纵深：淡彩与录音叠加，造出更厚的面。

branches.en: SYSTEM LEVELS: software and organizations stack parts that can be changed one at a time.
branches.cn: 系统层级：软件与组织叠起可逐层更换的部分。

branches.en: LAYERS OF MEANING: reading means peeling the stack apart.
branches.cn: 意义之层：阅读就是把这叠层剥开。

intro.en: Layering is an English formation from a native verb and two native suffixes, so its morphology is transparent.
intro.cn: layering 由本族动词加两个本族后缀构成，形态完全透明。

latinIntro.en: Lay has no Latin cognate, so latinEntries is left empty rather than given a guessed root.
latinIntro.cn: lay 没有拉丁同族词，因此 latinEntries 留空，不填猜测的词根。

items.example: A layer of dust covered the shelf.
The cake has a layered filling.
A clay interlayer seals the joint.
items.exampleCN: 一层黏土夹层封住接缝。

items.example: Layerage rooted the rose in a season.
items.exampleCN: 压条法使这株玫瑰一季生根。

definition_zh: v. （时间）消逝；过去；（期限）届满
definition_en: to slip by or pass, used only of time
core_image: 厨房计时器上的数字从三十跳到零，烤箱里的蛋糕已经鼓起来，孩子一直盯着那排数字；墙上日历被一页页撕下，桌角沙漏里的细沙只剩一小堆
scene: 厨房计时器上的数字从三十跳到零，烤箱里的蛋糕已经鼓起来，孩子一直盯着那排数字看。 Thirty minutes elapse before the timer reaches zero.
sceneCN: 这里 elapse 指「时间悄悄溜走、过去」（第 1 个义项：（时间）消逝）；句意是三十分钟过去，计时器才归零。图中可辨识物件：计时器数字、烤箱、鼓起的蛋糕。

senses.title: To slip away, of time
senses.definition: to slip by or pass, used only of time
senses.definitionCN: （动词）悄悄溜走、过去，只用于时间
senses.example: Thirty minutes elapse before the timer reaches zero.
senses.exampleCN: 三十分钟过去，计时器才归零。
senses.why: A kitchen timer counting down to zero while a cake rises behind the oven glass.
senses.whyCN: 厨房计时器倒数到零，烤箱玻璃后的蛋糕正在鼓起。

senses.title: To pass between events
senses.definition: to pass between one event and another
senses.definitionCN: （动词）在一件事与另一件事之间过去
senses.example: Two years elapsed between the first letter and the reply.
senses.exampleCN: 第一封信与回信之间过去了两年。
senses.why: Two envelopes on a desk with a torn calendar page lying between them.
senses.whyCN: 桌上两只信封，中间夹着一张撕下的日历页。

senses.title: To run out, of a period
senses.definition: to come to an end, used of a fixed period or deadline
senses.definitionCN: （动词）到期、结束，用于固定期限或截止日
senses.example: The offer lapsed once the thirty days had elapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 三十天一旦届满，那份报价就失效了。
senses.why: A printed deadline crossed out on a form beside a stamp gone dry.
senses.whyCN: 表格上印着的截止日被划掉，旁边一枚印章已经干涸。

intro.en: Elapse is Latin elapsus, slipped away, from elabi, which joins ex- meaning away to labi meaning to slip; the same laps- root gives lapse, collapse and relapse.
intro.cn: elapse 就是拉丁语 elapsus（已溜走的），来自 elabi，它把 ex-（离开）与 labi（滑动）结合；同一个 laps- 词根给出 lapse、collapse 与 relapse。

items.en: Latin labi means to slip or glide.
items.cn: 拉丁语 labi 意为滑动、溜走。

items.en: Adding ex- gives elabi, to slip away.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 elabi，意为溜走。

items.en: The participle elapsus means slipped away.
items.cn: 分词 elapsus 意为已溜走的。

items.en: English took elapse in the 15C, and only time could elapse.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借用 elapse，而且只有时间能 elapse。

items.en: The noun lapse named a slipping away of time or of duty.
items.cn: 名词 lapse 指时间或职责的悄悄流失。

items.en: Science used elapsed time for the interval measured on a clock.
items.cn: 科学用 elapsed time 指时钟量出的时间间隔。

note.en: Elapse, lapse and collapse all carry laps-, the Latin root for slipped; elapse is only for time, lapse adds the idea of a small failure.
note.cn: elapse、lapse 与 collapse 都带着 laps-，那是拉丁语「滑动」的词根；elapse 只用于时间，lapse 还多了「小失误」的意思。

entries.definition: to fall down or fail suddenly

entries.definition: the hiding of one body by another
entries.definitionCN: 食；使黯然失色

entries.definition: to go by, of time

dict_mnemonic.text: elapse ＝ e-（离开，ex- 的变体）＋ lapse（滑动，拉丁 labi／lapsus）＝「滑走」。关键限制：elapse 的主语只能是时间（time, years, minutes, hours），不能说「人 elapse」。同根一家：lapse 名词「小失误；（时间）流逝」，动词「失效」（membership lapses 会员资格失效）；collapse ＝ col-（一起）＋ lapse ＝ 一起滑倒＝倒塌、崩溃；relapse ＝ re-（回）＋ lapse ＝ 滑回去＝复发；elapsed 形容词「已过去的」，elapsed time 已用时间。日常口语说 time passes / time goes by，elapse 偏书面与计时语境。近义 expire 指「到期」（护照、合同），intervene 指「（时间）介于其间」。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（离开）＋ labi（滑动）→ elabi → elapsus（已溜走的）→ elapse（时间消逝）

senses.definition: taking place at the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与其他事同时进行
senses.example: The two courses run concurrent.

senses.title: Served at the same time

senses.example: He received concurrent sentences.

definition_zh: 改革；改良；宗教改革；（宗教改革形成的）新教运动
definition_en: the act or result of reforming something, especially the sixteenth-century movement that reshaped Western Christianity
core_image: 教堂大门上钉着一张列满条目的纸，门内是正被搬走的旧雕像，墙面重新刷成白色
scene: 十六世纪的印书坊里，刚装订好的小册子被一摞摞搬上马车，铅字盘还摊在案上。 Printing spread the reformation faster than any council could answer it.
sceneCN: 这里 reformation 指「十六世纪席卷西欧的宗教改革运动」（第 3 个义项：宗教改革这一历史事件）；句意为印刷术让宗教改革的传播快过任何一次宗教会议的回应。场景物件：小册子、铅字盘、马车、装订台。

senses.title: The act of reforming something
senses.definition: the process of changing a system, institution or practice for the better
senses.definitionCN: 把制度、机构或做法朝更好方向改变的过程
senses.example: The reformation of the tax code took three committees and two years.
senses.exampleCN: 税则的改革用了三个委员会和两年时间。
senses.why: reformatio is simply the noun of action from reformare 'to reshape', so any reshaping can carry the word.
senses.whyCN: reformatio 只是 reformare「重新塑形」的动作名词，因此任何重塑都能用这个词。

senses.title: The improved state produced
senses.titleCN: 改革后的状态、改良结果
senses.definition: the better condition that results from reform, seen as an outcome rather than a process
senses.definitionCN: 改革带来的较好状态，被看作结果而非过程
senses.example: The reformation of the prison was visible in its workshops, not its rules.
senses.exampleCN: 监狱的改良体现在车间里，而不在条文里。
senses.why: Latin nouns in -tio name both the doing and the thing done, and English kept that double face.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 -tio 名词同时指动作与所做之事，英语保留了这个双面性。

senses.title: The sixteenth-century Protestant movement
senses.titleCN: 十六世纪新教宗教改革
senses.definition: the movement that broke with the papacy and reshaped Western Christianity from 1517 onward
senses.definitionCN: 自 1517 年起与教廷决裂并重塑西欧基督教世界的运动
senses.example: Printing spread the reformation faster than any council could answer it.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术让宗教改革的传播快过任何一次宗教会议的回应。
senses.why: a general noun was captured by one event, and the capitalised form now names that event alone.
senses.whyCN: 一个普通名词被一次事件占据，大写形式如今只指那次事件。

senses.title: A wider religious reform movement
senses.titleCN: 更广泛的宗教改革运动
senses.definition: any organised drive to correct doctrine or discipline within a church, before or after the sixteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 十六世纪前后教会内部任何有组织的教义或纪律整顿
senses.example: The Gregorian reformation tightened rules on simony long before Luther.
senses.exampleCN: 格里高利改革在路德之前很久就收紧了买卖圣职的规定。
senses.why: historians needed the general sense to describe earlier reforms, so the same word serves several centuries.
senses.whyCN: 史家需要这层通义来描述更早的改革，同一个词于是服务好几个世纪。

senses.title: Correction of a person's conduct
senses.definition: the correction and retraining of an offender's habits, as in penal practice
senses.definitionCN: 对犯错者习惯的矫正与再训，如刑罚实践中的做法
senses.example: The judge sent him to a house of reformation rather than a prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法官把他送进感化院，而不是监狱。
senses.why: moral reshaping was part of the word from the start, and the prison system gave it an institution.
senses.whyCN: 道德上的重塑从一开始就在这个词里，监狱制度又给了它一个机构。

senses.title: Reform of an institution's rules
senses.definition: the revision of written rules, often in a university, army or religious order
senses.definitionCN: 对成文规章的修订，常见于大学、军队或修会
senses.example: The abbey's reformation of its rule cut the hours of manual work.
senses.exampleCN: 这座修道院对会规的改革削减了手工劳作的时间。
senses.why: the word prefers institutions with written constitutions, because reshaping needs a text to reshape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词偏爱有成文宪章的制度，因为要重塑就得有文本可塑。

senses.title: Used as a period label
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：宗教改革时期的
senses.definition: placed before a noun to mark something belonging to the Reformation era
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标出某物属于宗教改革时代
senses.example: Reformation theology put grace before merit and the sermon before the Mass.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教改革时期的神学把恩典放在功德之前，把讲道放在弥撒之前。
senses.why: English uses event names as modifiers, so an adjective is not needed to date a doctrine.
senses.whyCN: 英语把事件名直接作修饰语，因此无需形容词就能给教义标年代。

senses.title: Reform of spelling or writing
senses.definition: a deliberate change to the spelling or script of a language
senses.definitionCN: 对一种语言的拼法或文字所作的有意改变
senses.example: The reformation of Turkish spelling replaced Arabic letters with Latin ones in 1928.
senses.exampleCN: 土耳其的拼写改革在 1928 年用拉丁字母取代了阿拉伯字母。
senses.why: the general sense is productive, and language planners borrowed it for their own reshaping of texts.
senses.whyCN: 通义具有能产性，语言规划者便借它来描述自己对文本的重塑。

intro.en: Reformation goes back to Latin reformatio, the noun of reformare 'to form again', and it entered English first as a general word for improvement.
intro.cn: reformation 上承拉丁 reformatio，是 reformare「重新塑形」的名词，进入英语时先指一般的改良。

items.en: reformare 'to form again, reshape' joins re- 'again' to formare 'to form', itself from forma 'shape'.
items.cn: reformare「重新塑形」由 re-「再次」加 formare「成形」构成，后者出自 forma「形状」。

items.en: reformatio meant 'a reforming, a restoration', used of bringing something back to its proper earlier state.
items.cn: reformatio 意为「改革、复原」，用于把某物带回其原本恰当的状态。

items.en: English reformation is recorded in the early fifteenth century as a plain noun for correction or improvement.
items.cn: 英语 reformation 在 15 世纪初已有记录，作为普通的「纠正、改良」名词。

items.en: Through the fifteenth century the word was applied to calls for church reform, and after 1517 it named the movement itself.
items.cn: 整个 15 世纪这个词被用于呼求教会改革，1517 年之后则直接指那场运动。

items.en: Writers now capitalise Reformation for the historical event and keep the lowercase form for reform in general.
items.cn: 今人用大写 Reformation 指历史事件，小写形式留给一般意义的改革。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation is dated to the early fifteenth century, and the moment when the capitalised event sense settled differs from author to author.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语最早书证定在 15 世纪初；大写事件义何时稳定下来，各家说法不一。

note.en: Group one holds words on the same formare stock; group two holds the rival religious and political labels.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 formare 词干的词；第二组是竞争性的宗教与政治标签。

entries.definition: The verb and the everyday noun of improvement, without the historical weight of the long form.
entries.definitionCN: 动词与日常名词，指改良，没有长词形的历史分量。

entries.definition: From formare but with no re-, so it names the original making of something, such as a rock formation.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 formare 却没有 re-，指某物最初的生成，如岩层。

entries.definition: From informare 'to give shape to the mind', and unrelated to correction of abuses.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 informare「给心智赋形」，与矫正弊端无关。

entries.definition: The same root with de-, naming the loss or distortion of shape, the opposite of reform.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根加 de-，指形状的丧失或扭曲，与改革相反。

entries.definition: A change that replaces the whole order, usually by force; reform works inside the existing frame.
entries.definitionCN: 以整体取代旧秩序的变化，常伴武力；改革则在既有框架内进行。

entries.definition: A return of vitality rather than a change of rules, often used of cities or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 指活力的恢复而非规则的改变，常用于城市或信仰。

entries.definition: A narrower word for setting right a specific mistake, with no program of change.
entries.definitionCN: 较窄的词，指改正具体错误，不含整套变革纲领。

entries.definition: The Catholic response to the Protestant movement, built from the same noun with a prefix of opposition.
entries.definitionCN: 天主教对新教运动的回应，由同一名词加表对抗的前缀构成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin verb, a real suffix and real historical labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的后缀与真实的历史标签。

normal.en: re- 'again' + formare 'to shape' = to shape again, hence to reform.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ formare「塑形」= 重新塑形，也就是改革。

normal.en: forma 'shape' also gives form, formal, formation and formula.
normal.cn: forma「形状」还给出 form、formal、formation、formula。

normal.en: Capital R marks the event, lowercase r marks the process: the Reformation versus a reformation of taxes.
normal.cn: 大写 R 标事件，小写 r 标过程：宗教改革对税制改革。

normal.en: The date to hold is 1517, when the Ninety-Five Theses were printed and copied across Europe.
normal.cn: 要记住的年代是 1517 年，九十五条论纲被印出并传抄欧洲。

normal.en: Church, prison and spelling all take the word: each is a reshaping of an inherited text or habit.
normal.cn: 教会、监狱与拼写都能用这个词：三者都是对继承来的文本或习惯的重塑。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of grievances nailed to a door, still wet from the press.
abstract.cn: 想象一张刚下印刷机的诉状被钉在门上。

abstract.en: Picture a statue carried out of a church while whitewash goes on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一尊雕像被搬出教堂，白灰正刷上墙。

abstract.en: Picture a spelling book where every old letter has been crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一本拼写课本，每个旧字母都被划掉。

examples.en: The reformation of the civil service began with open examinations.
examples.cn: 文官制度的改革从公开考试开始。

examples.en: Historians date the Reformation from the printing of the theses in 1517.
examples.cn: 史家把宗教改革定在 1517 年论纲付印之时。

examples.en: The abbey's reformation of its rule shortened the daily offices.
examples.cn: 修道院对会规的改革缩短了每日的礼拜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞佛美申」听似「再佛一美」——把旧样子重新塑一遍 → 改革、宗教改革

root: 拉丁 reformatio「改革、复原」= re-「再次」+ formare「塑形」（出自 forma「形状」）+ -tio 动作名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture, shaping something again: an act, its result, the great religious reshaping, earlier church reforms, correction of persons, revision of rules, a period label, and even a spelling system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个动作——把某物重新塑一遍：行为、结果、那场宗教大重塑、更早的教会整顿、对人的矫正、规章的修订、时期标签，乃至一套拼写制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list nailed to a church door while old statues leave and the walls are whitewashed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸钉在教堂门上，旧雕像正被搬走，墙面重新刷白。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: the same -tio noun names the doing and the better state left behind.
branches.cn: 动作与结果：同一个名词既指做的过程，也指留下的较好状态。

branches.en: CHURCH: one event captured the word, yet the general sense still covers earlier reforms.
branches.cn: 教会：一次事件占住了这个词，通义却仍覆盖更早的改革。

branches.en: PERSONS AND RULES: moral correction of an offender and revision of a written constitution are both reshaping.
branches.cn: 人与规章：对犯错者的道德矫正与对成文宪章的修订，都是重塑。

branches.en: PERIOD LABEL: the event name works as a modifier, so doctrines can be dated without an adjective.
branches.cn: 时期标签：事件名可作修饰语，教义无需形容词就能标年代。

branches.en: TEXT: spelling reform carries the general sense into the alphabet itself.
branches.cn: 文本：拼写改革把通义带进字母表本身。

intro.en: Reformation is a Latin action noun whose pieces still build ordinary English words about shape.
intro.cn: reformation 是一个拉丁动作名词，它的各部件至今仍在构成关于「形状」的日常英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma 'shape' and formare 'to form' give form, formal, formation and reform; reformatio adds the action suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma「形状」与 formare「成形」给出 form、formal、formation、reform；reformatio 又加上动作后缀。

items.example: The prefix marks a second shaping.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出第二次塑形。

items.example: The root supplies the mould in every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为整个词族提供「模子」的意思。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The committee reformed the admissions rules.
items.exampleCN: 委员会改革了招生规则。

definition_en: a sudden sharp pain in a muscle, or to limit something

definition_zh: n. 冷漠；无兴趣；缺乏热情（尤指对公共事务）
definition_en: A lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern, especially about matters that most people think important; the state of not caring either way.
core_image: 心里那根弦松了，对什么都提不起劲
scene: 选民对这场辩论毫无反应，投票率低得惊人。 Voter apathy kept turnout below forty per cent.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apathy 指对本该关心的事提不起兴趣，voter apathy 就是选民懒得投票的那种集体冷淡。

senses.title: No interest or enthusiasm
senses.definition: a state in which someone feels no interest in or excitement about something that would normally matter
senses.definitionCN: 对本该在意的事情既不感兴趣也不激动的状态
senses.example: Apathy among students made the new club hard to launch.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们的冷淡让这个新社团很难办起来。
senses.why: The prefix a- means without and pathos means feeling, so the word literally names a state with the feeling removed.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「无」，pathos 意为「感受」，所以这个词字面上就是「把感受抽掉之后的状态」。

senses.title: No concern for public matters
senses.definition: the collective indifference of a group towards politics, charity or shared problems, the sense used in voter apathy
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体对政治、公益或共同问题集体性的不关心，即 voter apathy 中的用法
senses.example: The report blamed public apathy for the slow response to the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把洪灾应对迟缓归因于公众的冷漠。
senses.why: Here the feeling is not missing from one person but from a crowd, so apathy becomes a social problem rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺的不是一个人的感受，而是一整群人的感受，于是 apathy 从个人情绪变成了社会问题。

intro.en: Apathy comes from Greek apatheia, freedom from suffering, built from a-, without, and pathos, feeling. The Stoics admired it; English later turned it into a fault.
intro.cn: apathy 来自希腊语 apatheia「不受苦、无感」，由 a-「无」加 pathos「感受」构成。斯多葛学派把它当作修养，英语后来却把它变成了缺点。

items.en: Greek pathos meant suffering, and then feeling in general. It gives English pathos, sympathy, empathy and pathetic.
items.cn: 希腊语 pathos 意为「受苦」，进而泛指「感受」。它产生英语的 pathos、sympathy、empathy 与 pathetic。

items.en: Adding a-, without, gave apatheia, the Stoic goal of a mind unmoved by passion. It was praise, not blame.
items.cn: 加上 a-「无」得到 apatheia，即斯多葛派追求的「不为激情所动」的心境。这在当时是褒奖，不是指责。

items.en: Latin borrowed the term as apathia and kept it as a philosophical word for calm detachment.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 apathia，仍作为哲学术语，表示平静的超脱。

items.en: French apathie carried the word into Western Europe, where doctors began using it for a dull, unresponsive state.
items.cn: 法语 apathie 把这个词带入西欧，医生开始用它指一种呆滞、无反应的状态。

items.en: English took apathy around the 1590s, at first still meaning the philosophical calm the Stoics had praised.
items.cn: 英语在 1590 年代吸收 apathy，起初仍指斯多葛派赞赏的那种哲学式平静。

items.en: By 1733 the word had flipped: writers used apathy for indolence of mind, a failure to care that deserved criticism.
items.cn: 到 1733 年词义翻转：作者们用 apathy 指「心灵的怠惰」，成了该受批评的漠不关心。

note.en: The look-alike group centres on antipathy, which is active dislike rather than no feeling at all; the near-meaning group lists other words for not caring.
note.cn: 形近组的核心是 antipathy：那是主动的反感，而不是完全没有感受；近义组列出其他表示「不在意」的词。

entries.definition: A strong and settled dislike.

entries.definition: Feeling what another person feels.

entries.definition: Sharing or pitying another's feelings.

entries.definition: Showing no interest or effort.

entries.definition: Calm distance from involvement.

examples.en: His apathy towards the project worried the whole team.

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「无」+ pathy「感受」——心里没有感受，对什么都提不起劲，就是冷漠 apathy。

definition_zh: 开始；着手；开始存在；（仪式）开始
definition_en: to begin, especially in a formal or official way
core_image: 推开一扇门，跨过门槛，让一件事正式起步
scene: 奠基仪式上，铁锹落下第一铲土。 The first spadeful of soil was turned, and the construction work commenced.
sceneCN: 这里 commence 是「正式开始」（第 2 个义项：仪式或工程按程序启动）；句意：第一铲土落下，工程正式开始了。

senses.title: Begin an activity
senses.definition: to begin doing something, especially something planned or formal
senses.definitionCN: 开始做某事，尤指有计划或正式的事
senses.example: The meeting will commence at nine sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 会议将于九点整开始。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind it means 'to go in, enter'. To commence is to step across a threshold into an activity that now counts as begun.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁动词意为“走入、进入”。commence 就是跨过一道门槛，进入一件从此算作“已开始”的事。

senses.title: Start a ceremony or formal event
senses.definition: of a ceremony, ceremony, or public event, to open in the prescribed way
senses.definitionCN: （典礼或公共活动）按既定程序开场
senses.example: The graduation ceremony commenced with the national anthem.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼在国歌声中开始。
senses.why: Formal events have a marked entrance. Commence is the word for that moment when the ceremony leaves the waiting state and officially runs.
senses.whyCN: 正式活动有一个明确的“入场点”。commence 就指典礼离开等待状态、正式开始运转的那一刻。

senses.title: Take effect legally
senses.definition: of a contract, lease, or rule, to begin to have legal force
senses.definitionCN: （合同、租约或规则）开始具有法律效力
senses.example: The lease commences on the first of May.
senses.exampleCN: 租约自五月一日起生效。
senses.why: A contract also has a threshold: before a stated date it exists on paper but does nothing. Commencing is the moment it starts to bind the parties.
senses.whyCN: 合同也有一道门槛：在约定日期之前，它只在纸上存在，并不起作用。commence 就是它开始约束各方的时刻。

senses.title: Come into existence
senses.definition: of an era, process, or state, to begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: （时代、过程或状态）开始存在
senses.example: A new era of trade commenced after the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订后，贸易的新时代开始了。
senses.why: Here nothing is literally done by a person: a period opens. The verb describes the first point of a stretch of time rather than a first action.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不是某个人在做动作，而是一段时期打开了。动词描述的是时间段的第一个点，而不是第一个动作。

senses.title: Commence work or duty
senses.definition: to start work, duty, or a job, especially on a fixed date
senses.definitionCN: 开始工作、履职或上任，尤指在某个固定日期
senses.example: She commences duty as head nurse next Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 她下周一正式出任护士长。
senses.why: A post is a role someone enters. The word marks the crossing from appointee to office-holder, which is why it suits official appointments.
senses.whyCN: 职位是人“进入”的角色。这个词标记了从“被任命者”到“在职者”的跨越，因此适合正式任命。

senses.title: Commencement: the graduation ceremony
senses.definition: the noun commencement, in American English, the ceremony at which degrees are awarded
senses.definitionCN: 名词 commencement，在美式英语中指授予学位的毕业典礼
senses.example: Parents flew in for commencement.
senses.exampleCN: 父母专程飞来参加毕业典礼。
senses.why: The ceremony marks not the end of study but the beginning of the next stage. The noun keeps the verb's forward-facing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个典礼标记的不是学业的结束，而是下一阶段的开始。这个名词保留了动词“朝前看”的含义。

senses.title: Commence proceedings
senses.definition: to begin a legal action or official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 开始法律诉讼或正式程序
senses.example: The tenant commenced proceedings against the landlord.
senses.exampleCN: 租客对房东提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Legal procedure is a sequence with a formal first step. Commencing names that step, so the phrase is fixed in court language.
senses.whyCN: 法律程序是一套有正式第一步的序列。commence 命名了那一步，因此这个搭配在法庭语言里是固定的。

senses.title: Commencing: opening or initial
senses.definition: the present participle used attributively, meaning opening or initial
senses.definitionCN: 现在分词作定语，表示“开端的、起初的”
senses.example: The commencing chapter sets out the main argument.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇那一章提出了主要论点。
senses.why: The participle captures the first moment as it happens. Used before a noun, it labels whatever stands at the entrance of a sequence.
senses.whyCN: 现在分词捕捉正在发生的“第一刻”。放在名词前，它就标注处于序列入口的那个东西。

intro.en: Commence is a French-shaped verb built on a Latin beginning. The 'entering' image is visible in its Latin ancestors, and the graduation sense is an American development.
intro.cn: commence 是一个法语形的动词，建立在拉丁语“开始”之上。“进入”的意象在其拉丁语祖先里看得见，毕业典礼义则是美式英语的发展。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning', and inire meant 'to go in, enter, begin'. The physical image is stepping inside.
items.cn: initium 意为“开端”，inire 意为“走入、进入、开始”。其具体意象是“迈步进入”。

items.en: A reconstructed *cominitiare added com- 'together' as an intensifier to initiare 'to begin'. The com- does not mean 'with someone' here; it strengthens the start.
items.cn: 重构形式 *cominitiare 在 initiare“开始”前加了加强语气的 com-。这里的 com- 不是“与人一起”，而是强化“开始”这一动作。

items.en: Old French comencier, commencier (11c.) carried the word into everyday French with the sense 'to begin'.
items.cn: 古法语 comencier、commencier（11 世纪）把这个词带入日常法语，意为“开始”。

items.en: English took commence from French in the 14th century. It has always sounded more formal than begin, which is native English.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪从法语借入 commence。它一直比本族语的 begin 更正式。

items.en: Commencement for the degree ceremony is a 19th-century American usage. The idea is that the ceremony begins the graduate's new life rather than closing their studies.
items.cn: 用 commencement 指学位授予典礼，是 19 世纪的美式用法。其理据是：典礼开启毕业生的新生活，而不是结束学业。

items.en: Modern usage keeps commence for ceremonies, contracts, works, and legal proceedings. Begin and start cover the ordinary, informal cases.
items.cn: 现代用法把 commence 留给典礼、合同、工程与法律程序；日常非正式场合则由 begin 和 start 承担。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the buying and selling of goods. It shares the comm- opening but comes from merx 'merchandise', not from 'begin'.
entries.definitionCN: 商业；贸易。同样以 comm- 开头，但来自 merx“商品”，与“开始”无关。

entries.definition: a remark or explanation. It shares the opening syllables but comes from a verb meaning 'to devise, think'.
entries.definitionCN: 评论；说明。开头音节相近，但来自意为“构思、思考”的动词。

entries.definition: to praise or recommend. It is close in sound but means handing something over with approval.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；推荐。读音接近，但意思是带着认可把某物交出去。

entries.definition: a beginning, or the graduation ceremony. It is the noun built directly on commence.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；毕业典礼。它是直接由 commence 构成的名词。

entries.definition: to start doing something. It is the ordinary native word, with no special formality.
entries.definitionCN: 开始。最普通的本族词，不带正式色彩。

entries.definition: to begin, often with a sense of setting something in motion. It is more physical and less ceremonial than commence.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；启动。更偏“让某物动起来”，不如 commence 正式。

entries.definition: to cause a process to begin. It stresses the first push rather than the ceremony of opening.
entries.definitionCN: 发起；启动。强调最初的一推，而不是开场仪式。

entries.definition: to start something publicly, especially a product or campaign. It adds publicity to the beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 正式推出；发起。在“开始”之外增加了公开宣传的意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin initium 'beginning', the French form of the verb, and the fixed phrases in which English still prefers commence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 initium“开端”、该动词的法语形式，以及英语仍偏好用 commence 的固定搭配。

normal.en: commence and initiate are cousins: both sit on Latin initium 'a beginning', which pictures a person stepping inside.
normal.cn: commence 与 initiate 是远亲：两者都建立在拉丁语 initium“开端”上，意象是“人迈步进入”。

normal.en: Commence is the formal twin of begin: meetings, ceremonies, contracts and court proceedings commence.
normal.cn: commence 是 begin 的正式孪生兄弟：会议、典礼、合同与法庭程序都用 commence。

normal.en: A lease commences on a date, because the contract crosses its threshold at that moment.
normal.cn: 租约在某日 commence，因为合同就在那一刻跨过自己的门槛。

normal.en: Commencement is the American graduation ceremony: it opens the next stage rather than closing the school years.
normal.cn: commencement 是美式毕业典礼：它开启下一阶段，而不是给学校岁月画句号。

normal.en: Commencing work means crossing from preparation into production, which is why factories and sites use the word.
normal.cn: commencing work 指从准备跨入生产，因此工厂与工地爱用这个词。

abstract.en: The core picture is a door: the activity already exists behind it, and commence is the act of stepping through.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一扇门：活动早就在门后存在，commence 是跨过去的那一步。

abstract.en: The word always looks forward: what is commencing is not the old state but the new one that has just been entered.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是朝前看：正在 commence 的不是旧状态，而是刚刚被进入的新状态。

abstract.en: Formality is the word's social dress: the same threshold is crossed by begin in speech and by commence in documents.
abstract.cn: 正式性是这个词的社会外衣：同一道门槛，口语用 begin 跨，文件用 commence 跨。

examples.en: Construction will commence as soon as the permit is issued.
examples.cn: 许可证一经签发，工程就会开工。

examples.en: The course commences with a short diagnostic test.
examples.cn: 这门课以一次简短的诊断测试开始。

examples.en: Her contract commences in September and runs for two years.
examples.cn: 她的合同九月生效，为期两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可门寺」——寺门一开，法会正式开始 → commence 开始

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开端”、inire“走入、开始”，经俗拉丁语 *cominitiare 与古法语 comencier 进入英语，核心是“跨进门、正式起步”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of commence, all organised around a threshold. An activity, a ceremony, a contract, an era, a post, a degree ceremony, a lawsuit, and an opening chapter each have their own moment of stepping through.
sensesIntro.cn: commence 的八个义项都围绕一道门槛组织：一项活动、一场典礼、一份合同、一个时代、一个职位、一次毕业典礼、一场诉讼、开篇一章，各自都有跨过去的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door already open, and the step that carries someone across the threshold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇已经打开的门，以及把人带过门槛的那一步。

branches.en: THE FIRST STEP: an activity or a first chapter is what lies just inside the door.
branches.cn: 第一步：门内最近的东西，是一项活动或开篇一章。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC OPENING: ceremonies and graduations are entrances performed in front of others.
branches.cn: 公开开场：典礼与毕业式是在众人面前完成的“入场”。

branches.en: FORMAL FORCE: a contract or a lawsuit starts to bind only when its stated threshold is crossed.
branches.cn: 正式效力：合同或诉讼只有跨过既定门槛，才开始产生约束力。

branches.en: A PERIOD OPENS: an era commences without any person acting, because time itself is the thing that starts.
branches.cn: 时期开启：时代自行 commence，无需某个人动手，因为开始的是时间本身。

branches.en: A ROLE BEGINS: taking up a post is entering a chair that already exists.
branches.cn: 角色开始：上任就是进入一把早已存在的椅子。

intro.en: Commence carries the Latin beginning initium inside it. English adds -ment to make the noun and -ing to make the participle; the prefix com- here only intensifies.
intro.cn: commence 内部携带着拉丁语“开端”initium。英语加 -ment 构成名词，加 -ing 构成分词；这里的 com- 只起加强语气作用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around initium is large and still productive in English: initial, initiative, initiate, initiation, and the verb inire 'to go in'.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 initium 的拉丁词族很大，在英语里仍有生产力：initial、initiative、initiate、initiation，以及动词 inire“走入”。

items.meaningCN: 开始；正式着手（com- 表加强，initiare 表“开始”）
开始；毕业典礼（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: Commencement is held on the main lawn.
items.exampleCN: 毕业典礼在主草坪上举行。

items.meaningCN: 开端的；起初的（-ing 构成现在分词）
items.example: The commencing phase lasts two weeks.

items.exampleCN: 最初的结果看起来不错。

items.meaning: to set a process going; to admit someone into a group
items.example: They initiated a review of the policy.
items.exampleCN: 他们启动了对这项政策的审查。

items.meaning: the act of starting, or a formal admission
items.meaningCN: 发起；入会仪式（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The initiation of the project took a month.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目的启动花了一个月。

items.meaning: the ability to act first; a new plan
items.meaningCN: 主动性；新倡议（-ative 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: She took the initiative to call a meeting.
items.exampleCN: 她主动发起了一次会议。

items.meaning: the beginning of an institution or project
items.meaningCN: 开端；创立（in-“进入”+ capere“拿取”，同表“起始”）
items.example: The club has grown since its inception.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部自创立以来不断壮大。

definition_zh: 激增；迅速扩散；增殖；繁殖；增生；使激增
definition_en: to increase rapidly in number, to spread widely through an area, or to reproduce and multiply
core_image: 浅水塘里起初只有几簇绿藻，几天后整片水面都被覆盖，边缘还不断冒出新芽
scene: 浅水塘起初只有几簇绿藻，三天后整片水面都染成绿色，边缘还在向外蔓延。 Algae proliferate across the pond within days.
sceneCN: 这里指数量在短时间内迅速变多并铺开（第 1 个义项：数量迅速激增）；句意为藻类在数日内遍布整个池塘。图中可辨识物件：浅水塘、绿色藻簇、向外扩散的水纹。

pos.zh: 激增；扩散；增殖；繁殖；使激增

collocations.zh: 在温暖水域中大量繁殖

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「增殖；激增；扩散」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「增殖性的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「不断增殖的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「增殖者；促增殖物」

senses.title: To rise sharply in number
senses.definition: to increase rapidly in number within a short span of time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内数量迅速变多
senses.example: Online orders proliferate in the weeks before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 节前几周，线上订单迅速激增。
senses.why: The Latin verb first described offspring arriving one after another, and a sudden surge of any countable thing repeats that picture of many new copies.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词最初描述后代接连出生，任何可计数之物突然涌来，都重复了「新副本大量出现」的画面。

senses.title: To spread quickly through an area
senses.definition: to spread over a wide area in a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内向广大区域铺开
senses.example: Rumours proliferate across social platforms within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言在数小时内传遍社交平台。
senses.why: Once copies multiply, they also move outward, so the word covers spatial spread as well as number.
senses.whyCN: 副本一旦增多，也会向外移动，因此这个词既指数目，也指空间上的铺开。

senses.title: To multiply by cell division
senses.definition: to increase in number by repeated division of cells
senses.definitionCN: 通过细胞反复分裂而数目增多
senses.example: The cells proliferate rapidly in the warm culture.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞在温暖的培养液中迅速增殖。
senses.why: Biology took the word for producing offspring and applied it to single cells producing more of themselves.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个表示「产生后代」的词用于单细胞自我复制。

senses.title: To breed and multiply
senses.definition: to reproduce and build up a larger population
senses.definitionCN: 繁殖并使种群数量增大
senses.example: These fish proliferate in shallow, weed-filled ponds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鱼在长满水草的浅塘里大量繁殖。
senses.why: Plants and animals were the first subjects of the word, and population growth keeps the original sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 动植物是这个词最早的描述对象，种群增长让本义一直延续。

senses.title: To grow abnormally in tissue
senses.definition: to grow beyond the normal amount, especially in body tissue
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指身体组织超出正常范围地生长
senses.example: Abnormal cells proliferate in the lining of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 异常细胞在胃壁内层增生。
senses.why: When division escapes control, the same multiplying word describes a medical danger rather than healthy growth.
senses.whyCN: 当分裂失去控制，同一个表示「增多」的词就描述医学上的危险，而非健康生长。

senses.title: To flood a medium with copies
senses.definition: to appear in very large numbers as texts, images or reports
senses.definitionCN: 以文本、图像或报道的形式大量出现
senses.example: Cheap copies of the report proliferate on the web.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的廉价副本在网上大量涌现。
senses.why: Digital copying made the word natural for information, where every duplicate is a new offspring.
senses.whyCN: 数字复制让这个词自然用于信息，因为每一份副本都像一个新后代。

senses.title: To send out new branches
senses.definition: to form new shoots, branches or vessels that extend from an existing structure
senses.definitionCN: 从既有结构上长出新枝、新分支或新血管
senses.example: New vessels proliferate around the damaged tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 新的血管在受损组织周围增生。
senses.why: Botany supplied the earliest English use, where a plant proliferates by putting out fresh growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学提供了这个词最早的英语用法：植物靠长出新芽而增殖。

senses.title: To cause to multiply
senses.definition: to make something increase in number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的数量或总量增多
senses.example: A rich medium proliferates the bacteria within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 营养丰富的培养基能在数小时内使细菌大量增殖。
senses.why: The transitive use adds a cause to the picture: something supplies the conditions, and the copies follow.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法在画面里加了一个原因：某物提供条件，副本便随之增多。

intro.en: Proliferate comes from Latin proles, offspring, and ferre, to carry or bring, through the adjective prolifer, bringing offspring, and the verb proliferare, to produce offspring.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「proles」后代与「ferre」携带、产生，先构成形容词「prolifer」带来后代的，再构成动词「proliferare」产生后代、繁殖。

items.en: Proles named offspring and descendants, the young produced by a family or a species.
items.cn: 这个词指后代与子孙，即家庭或物种所生育的幼体。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, bring or produce, and it supplied the second half of the word.
items.cn: 这个词意为携带、带来或产生，构成了该词的后半部分。

items.en: The adjective described a parent or a plant that brings offspring into being.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述能带来后代的亲体或植物。

items.en: The verb meant to produce offspring and to keep breeding.
items.cn: 这个动词意为产生后代、不断繁殖。

items.en: English adopted the word through botanical writing, where plants proliferate by producing new growth.
items.cn: 英语经植物学著作引入这个词，指植物靠长出新枝而增殖。

items.en: In the late twentieth century the word widened to any rapid increase, from cells to rumours.
items.cn: 到二十世纪后期，这个词扩展为泛指任何迅速增多，从细胞到谣言。

note.en: The first group looks like proliferate or shares its stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of multiplying and spreading.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「proliferate」相近或共享词干；第二组是与「增多、扩散」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of multiplying or spreading.
entries.definitionCN: 指增殖或扩散的过程。

entries.definition: Adjective describing tissue or cells that keep dividing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不断分裂的组织或细胞。

entries.definition: A person or agent that causes something to multiply.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物大量增多的人或因素。

entries.definition: Bearing many offspring or buds; an older adjective from the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: 指多产、多芽的；是同一拉丁词族中较老的形容词。

entries.definition: Highly productive; its second half comes from Latin facere, to make, not from ferre.
entries.definitionCN: 指多产的；后半出自拉丁语「facere」制造，而不是「ferre」。

entries.definition: To grow in number by natural increase or by repeated copying.
entries.definitionCN: 指因自然增多或反复复制而数量变大。

entries.definition: To extend over a wider area or among more people.
entries.definitionCN: 指向更大范围或更多人群扩展。

entries.definition: To become more intense or larger, often used of problems and conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指程度或规模升级，常用于问题与冲突。

entries.definition: To grow or appear very quickly, like mushrooms after rain.
entries.definitionCN: 指像雨后蘑菇一样迅速生长或出现。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin offspring image, the real word family and the usual subjects of the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语的后代意象、真实同族词与这个词的常见搭配对象。

normal.en: The Latin proles is offspring and ferre is to bring, so proliferate is literally to bring offspring forth.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「proles」是后代，「ferre」是带来：这个词字面上就是「把后代带出来」。

normal.en: Proliferation, proliferative and proliferous all keep the same picture of new copies.
normal.cn: 增殖、增殖性的与多产的都保留着「新副本不断出现」的画面。

normal.en: Cells proliferate, weeds proliferate and rumours proliferate: the subject only has to be countable and fast.
normal.cn: 细胞增殖、杂草蔓延、谣言疯传：主语只要可计数且速度快就行。

normal.en: Proliferate rapidly is the plainest collocation, and it fits algae, orders and copies alike.
normal.cn: 「proliferate rapidly」是最朴素的搭配，藻类、订单与副本都适用。

normal.en: Botanists used the word before economists did, so a plant putting out shoots is the cleanest picture.
normal.cn: 植物学家比经济学家更早使用这个词，因此植物抽枝是最干净的画面。

abstract.en: Every duplicate is a child of the original, and the word counts them all at once.
abstract.cn: 每一份副本都是原件的孩子，而这个词把它们一次数完。

abstract.en: Rumour proliferates because retelling is breeding; each listener becomes a new parent.
abstract.cn: 谣言会蔓延，因为复述就是繁殖；每个听者都成了新的亲本。

abstract.en: Unchecked division is growth in one frame and danger in another, and the word does not judge.
abstract.cn: 不受控制的分裂，在一个框架里是生长，在另一个框架里是危险，而这个词不作判断。

examples.en: Weeds proliferate once the field is left untended.
examples.cn: 田地一旦无人打理，杂草便迅速蔓延。

examples.en: False listings proliferate on auction sites before the holidays.
examples.cn: 节前，虚假商品信息在拍卖网站上大量涌现。

examples.en: Stem cells proliferate under the right chemical signals.
examples.cn: 干细胞在合适的化学信号下增殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普若利福瑞特」——后代一茬接一茬地生出来，数目越滚越大：激增、增殖

root: 拉丁语「proles」意为后代，加上「ferre」携带、产生，先构成形容词「prolifer」带来后代的，再构成动词「proliferare」产生后代、繁殖；英语十九世纪经植物学引入，二十世纪后期扩为泛指激增。注意同根词「prolific」后半出自「facere」制造，与「ferre」不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from pure number to living growth: a sharp rise, wide spread, cell division, breeding, abnormal tissue, a flood of copies, new branches, and a transitive cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从纯数目走向生命生长：数量激增、广泛扩散、细胞分裂、繁殖增多、组织增生、副本涌现、新生分支，以及及物的使增殖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one patch of algae sends out new shoots until the whole pond is green.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小片藻类不断分出新芽，直到整片池塘变绿。

branches.en: THE PURE SURGE: the number climbs fast, with no stated limit and no stated cause.
branches.cn: 纯数量激增：数目快速上升，既未说明限度，也未说明原因。

branches.en: THE OUTWARD SPREAD: the same copies also move across space and media.
branches.cn: 向外扩散：同样的副本也在空间与媒介上移动。

branches.en: THE LIVING MULTIPLICATION: cells divide, and plants and animals add to their populations.
branches.cn: 生命增殖：细胞分裂，动植物扩大种群。

branches.en: THE GROWING BODY: tissue and vessels put out new growth, healthy or not.
branches.cn: 身体生长：组织与血管长出新结构，无论健康与否。

branches.en: THE COPY AND THE CAUSE: texts flood a medium, and a cause makes the number rise.
branches.cn: 副本与原因：文本淹没媒介，而某个原因使数目上升。

intro.en: Proliferate is built from a Latin noun of offspring and a Latin verb of carrying, and its endings are ordinary verb and noun endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示后代的拉丁名词与一个表示携带的拉丁动词构成，词尾是普通的动词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies proles, ferre, the adjective prolifer and the verb proliferare; the English forms add only the usual endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「proles」「ferre」以及形容词「prolifer」和动词「proliferare」；英语形式只加了常用词尾。

items.example: The noun names the young of a family or a species.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指家庭或物种的幼体。

items.meaning: to carry; to bring; to produce
items.example: The verb supplies the carrying half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了「携带」那一半。

items.structure: Latin adjective from proles and ferre
items.example: The adjective stands between the noun and the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词位于名词与动词之间。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The ending marks the English verb of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标明英语动作动词。

items.meaning: the act or result of multiplying
full of; having the quality of
items.example: It forms the older adjective proliferous.

由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「增殖性的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「不断增殖的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「增殖者」

definition_zh: n. 缺乏；短缺；不足
definition_en: a state in which there is not enough of something that is needed
core_image: 货架空了一大半，想要的那样东西偏偏没有
scene: 证据太少，案子立不住。 There was a dearth of evidence, so the case failed.
sceneCN: 第 3 个义项：dearth 指信息不足；句意是证据太少，案子立不住。

senses.title: Not enough supply
senses.definition: a shortage of goods such as food or water
senses.definitionCN: 食物、水等物资的短缺
senses.example: The war caused a dearth of grain.
senses.exampleCN: 战争造成了粮食短缺。
senses.why: An empty shelf where the goods should be.
senses.whyCN: 本该摆满货品的空货架。

senses.title: Hard to find
senses.definition: a lack of people or skills that are needed
senses.definitionCN: 所需人手或技能的缺乏
senses.example: There is a dearth of trained nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 受过训练的护士很缺。
senses.why: A post that nobody comes to fill.
senses.whyCN: 一个没人来填补的岗位。

senses.title: Too little information
senses.definition: a lack of facts, proof or news about something
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的事实、证据或消息不足

items.cn: deore 意为珍贵或昂贵。

items.en: Derthe meant dearness, the state of being costly.
items.cn: derthe 意为昂贵，即代价高的状态。

items.en: The ending -th made nouns from adjectives.
items.cn: 词尾 -th 把形容词变成名词。

items.en: Costly goods were hard to get, so derthe came to mean scarcity.
items.cn: 昂贵的东西难买到，derthe 于是有了短缺义。

items.en: Dearth was used for famine and poor harvests.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dearth 用于饥荒与歉收。

items.en: Dearth is used for any lack, such as evidence.
items.cn: 二十世纪 dearth 用于任何缺乏，如证据不足。

definition_zh: 大哭；喊叫；大声训斥
definition_en: to cry out loudly and unrestrainedly; to shout; to shout at someone
core_image: 婴儿憋足了劲的嚎啕，整个屋子都听得见
scene: 儿科诊室里针头刚落下，孩子的哭声掀翻屋顶。 The toddler began to bawl the moment the shot was given.
sceneCN: 这里 bawl 指「嚎啕大哭」（第 1 个义项：放声大哭）；句意：针一打下去，幼儿就嚎啕大哭起来。

senses.title: To cry loudly
senses.definition: to cry out noisily and without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 毫无节制地大声哭喊
senses.example: The baby bawled all through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿哭闹了一整夜。
senses.why: Middle English bawlen meant to bark or howl: the mouth opens wide.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 bawlen 意为吠、嚎：嘴张到最大。

senses.title: To shout
senses.definition: to call out in a loud, rough voice
senses.definitionCN: 以粗大的嗓门呼喊
senses.example: Vendors bawled their prices across the square.
senses.exampleCN: 小贩们在广场上高声叫卖。
senses.why: The same wide-open mouth serves outrage or commerce.
senses.whyCN: 同一张大嘴，既可宣泄，也可做买卖。

senses.title: To scold loudly
senses.definition: to shout at someone in anger
senses.definitionCN: 怒气冲冲地对人吼叫
senses.example: The sergeant bawled out the recruit.
senses.exampleCN: 中士把新兵臭骂一顿。
senses.why: Anger borrows the volume of grief.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒借用悲嚎的音量。

senses.title: Cattle bawling
senses.definition: of cattle, to cry loudly, as in hunger or distress
senses.definitionCN: 指牛因饥饿或不安而哞叫
senses.example: The calves bawled for their mothers.
senses.exampleCN: 小牛哞哞叫着找母牛。
senses.why: The bark-word suits animals best of all.
senses.whyCN: 吠嚎之词最宜于牲畜。

senses.title: Bawl out idiom
senses.definition: to reprimand severely
senses.definitionCN: 严厉训斥
senses.example: I got bawled out for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 我因迟到被臭骂一顿。
senses.why: The scolding sense fixed into a phrasal verb.
senses.whyCN: 训斥义固化为短语动词。

senses.title: To bawl one's eyes out
senses.titleCN: 习语 bawl one's eyes out
senses.definition: to cry extremely hard
senses.definitionCN: 痛哭不止
senses.example: She bawled her eyes out at the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 她在葬礼上哭得死去活来。
senses.why: The idiom exaggerates crying into loss.
senses.whyCN: 习语把哭夸张成「哭掉眼睛」。

senses.title: Figurative public outcry
senses.definition: to protest loudly in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合高声抗议
senses.example: Crowds bawled for fair prices.
senses.exampleCN: 人群高喊要求公平价格。
senses.why: Collective mouths open like one.
senses.whyCN: 众口一张，同声一呼。

senses.title: Bawling of newborns
senses.definition: the first loud cries at birth
senses.definitionCN: 出生时的第一声啼哭
senses.example: The delivery room waited for the first bawl.
senses.exampleCN: 产房里所有人都在等第一声啼哭。
senses.why: Life announces itself at full volume.
senses.whyCN: 生命以最大音量宣告到场。
