definition_zh: 贸易自由化；削减关税与贸易壁垒、让商品与服务更自由跨境流动的政策过程
definition_en: the policy process of lowering tariffs and removing other barriers so that goods and services can cross borders more freely
core_image: 海关大厅里，一整页税目被逐行划掉，闸口抬起，货车不再停车受检
scene: 海关大厅里，官员把一整页税目表逐行划掉，闸口抬起，排队的货车直接通过。 Years of trade liberalization cut the average tariff from forty percent to under five.
sceneCN: 这里指「削减关税与壁垒、让商品更自由跨境流动的政策过程」，对应第 1 个义项：以降低关税为主线的开放过程；句意为多年的贸易自由化把平均关税从四成降到不足五个百分点。画面要点：海关柜台、税目表、抬起的闸杆。

pos.zh: 贸易自由化（指政策过程，也可指某一轮具体的开放举措）

forms.label: 复数（指多轮或多国举措）
形容词（开放的；自由派的）

derivatives.zh: 自由化（单独使用时多指经济领域的放开）
开放的；自由派的 / 自由派人士

senses.title: Cutting tariffs
senses.definition: the reduction of duties charged on imported goods, usually in scheduled steps
senses.definitionCN: 降低对进口货物征收的税，通常按预定步骤分阶段进行
senses.example: Trade liberalization halved the duty on machine tools.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易自由化把机床的关税降了一半。
senses.why: liberal here carries its oldest political meaning of 'free', so the phrase names the removal of a charge that restricts entry.
senses.whyCN: liberal 在这里取它最古老的政治含义「自由的」，因此这个短语指的是取消那道限制进入的收费。

senses.title: Taking non-tariff barriers down
senses.definition: the removal of quotas, licensing rules and discriminatory standards that block imports without a duty
senses.definitionCN: 取消配额、许可证规则与歧视性标准，这些手段不征税却同样挡住进口
senses.example: The talks moved from tariffs to trade liberalization of licensing rules.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判从关税推进到许可证规则层面的贸易自由化。
senses.why: once duties fall, the remaining obstacles are administrative, and the same phrase extends to them because the goal is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 关税降下之后，剩下的障碍是行政性的；目标未变，所以同一个短语也扩用到这些障碍上。

senses.title: A multilateral negotiating round
senses.titleCN: 多边谈判中的一轮开放
senses.definition: a package of reciprocal concessions agreed by many countries at once
senses.definitionCN: 许多国家同时达成的一揽子互惠让步
senses.example: The Uruguay Round was the broadest trade liberalization of its decade.
senses.exampleCN: 乌拉圭回合是那个十年里范围最广的一次贸易自由化。
senses.why: concessions are traded rather than given, so the word regularly names a round in which each country pays with its own barriers.
senses.whyCN: 让步是交换来的而不是白给的，因此这个词常指一轮谈判，各国都用自己的壁垒来付账。

senses.title: One country opening alone
senses.definition: the lowering of a country's own barriers without waiting for partners to match it
senses.definitionCN: 本国先降低壁垒，不等贸易伙伴作出对等回应
senses.example: Unilateral trade liberalization surprised its trading partners.
senses.exampleCN: 单边贸易自由化让它的贸易伙伴感到意外。
senses.why: the phrase needs an adjective to say whether the opening was bargained or done alone, and unilateral marks the second case.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语需要形容词来说明开放是换来的还是单做的，而「单边」正标记后一种情况。

senses.title: Extending it to services and investment
senses.titleCN: 把开放扩展到服务与投资
senses.definition: the application of the same logic to banking, transport, telecoms and foreign direct investment
senses.definitionCN: 把同一套逻辑用于银行、运输、电信与外国直接投资
senses.example: Modern trade liberalization covers services as much as goods.
senses.exampleCN: 当代的贸易自由化对服务的覆盖不亚于货物。
senses.why: goods were only the first frontier; the same reasoning about entry barriers applies to a foreign bank or a foreign investor.
senses.whyCN: 货物只是第一道前沿；关于进入壁垒的同一套推理，同样适用于一家外国银行或一位外国投资者。

senses.title: A package with adjustment costs
senses.titleCN: 带着调整代价的政策组合
senses.definition: an opening programme that also involves compensation, retraining or phased timetables for affected firms
senses.definitionCN: 在开放的同时安排补偿、再培训或分阶段时间表，以照顾受影响的行业
senses.example: The agreement paired trade liberalization with aid for displaced workers.
senses.exampleCN: 该协定把贸易自由化与对失业工人的援助配在一起。
senses.why: opening creates losers as well as winners, so in policy speech the word often carries the price tag attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 开放既造赢家也造输家，因此在政策话语中这个词常连带标出它要付的代价。

senses.title: The measured result: a rising trade share
senses.titleCN: 可测量的结果：贸易占比上升
senses.definition: the observable rise in imports and exports relative to national income after barriers fall
senses.definitionCN: 壁垒下降后，进出口相对于国民收入可观察到的上升
senses.example: Trade liberalization showed up in the data as a jump in exports.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易自由化在数据上表现为出口的跃升。
senses.why: a policy is judged by its trace in statistics, so the same noun can denote the outcome as well as the decision.
senses.whyCN: 政策要靠统计留下的痕迹来评判，因此同一个名词既能指决定，也能指结果。

senses.title: Abstract: freeing exchange from restriction
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：让交换摆脱限制
senses.definition: in general use, the loosening of any rules that restrict the exchange of goods, ideas or people
senses.definitionCN: 泛指放松限制货物、观念或人员交换的规则
senses.example: The same argument for liberalization appears in debates about academic exchange.
senses.exampleCN: 支持自由化的同一套论证也出现在关于学术交流的讨论里。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the movement from restriction to openness and lets the trade content fall away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「从限制走向开放」这一动向，贸易内容则被抽走。

intro.en: Trade liberalization joins an English commercial noun of Low German origin to a Latin adjective for freedom, with a noun suffix that came through French from Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trade liberalization 把一个源自低地德语的英语商业名词，与一个表示自由的拉丁形容词连在一起，再加一个经法语来自希腊语的抽象名词后缀。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trade first meant 'track, course' and entered English in the fourteenth century as a word for a path or a habitual way; the commercial sense 'exchange of goods' is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: trade 最初意为「路径、走向」，十四世纪进入英语时指道路或惯常做法；表示「货物交换」的商业义从十六世纪起有书证。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, not enslaved' and also 'unrestricted'; its deeper origin is not settled, so any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、非奴役的」，也指「不受限制的」；它更深的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Liberalis meant 'of a free man, generous', and English took it as liberal in the fourteenth century with the sense of giving freely.
items.cn: liberalis 意为「自由人的、慷慨的」，英语在十四世纪以 liberal 借入，带「慷慨给予」的意思。

items.en: By the nineteenth century liberal had shifted in economic writing to mean free of state restriction, and the verb liberalize and the noun liberalization were coined on that sense.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，liberal 在经济文献中已转为「不受国家限制的」，动词 liberalize 与名词 liberalization 就按这个义项造出。

items.en: The full phrase became standard after 1945 in negotiations over tariffs, where each round was described as a step of trade liberalization.
items.cn: 这一完整说法在 1945 年之后的关税谈判中成为标准用语，每一轮都被称为贸易自由化的一步。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin root of liber is disputed, and the earliest use of the full phrase is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：liber 在拉丁语之前的词根存在争议，这一完整短语的最早用例只能给出约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like liberalization but mean something else; group two holds policies and outcomes that are often mentioned in the same sentence.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 liberalization 而含义不同的词；第二组是常与它出现在同一句话里的政策与结果。

entries.definition: The freeing of a person or a territory from control; it shares the root of freedom but not the economic subject.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或领土摆脱控制而获自由；同出「自由」词根，但对象不是经济。

entries.definition: A political philosophy stressing individual rights and limited government; trade policy is only one application of it.
entries.definitionCN: 强调个人权利与有限政府的政治哲学；贸易政策只是它的一个应用。

entries.definition: The quality of giving freely or thinking broadly; it is a personal trait, not a programme of tariff cuts.
entries.definitionCN: 指慷慨给予或心胸开阔的品质；属个人特质，不是削减关税的方案。

entries.definition: An adjective for a market or rule that has already been freed; the phrase names the act of freeing it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已经放开的行业或规则；而本词短语指放开这一动作。

entries.definition: Exchange with no barriers at all; liberalization is the movement toward that state and may stop short of it.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有壁垒的交换；自由化是朝这一状态走的过程，未必走到终点。

entries.definition: The removal of internal rules on prices or entry; it concerns a home market rather than border measures.
entries.definitionCN: 取消国内关于价格或准入的规则；针对本国市场，而非边境措施。

entries.definition: The right for foreign suppliers to sell into a market; access is what liberalization is meant to deliver.
entries.definitionCN: 外国供应商进入某市场销售的权利；准入正是自由化要交付的东西。

entries.definition: The plain-language term for letting outsiders in; it is vaguer and can cover investment, culture and information too.
entries.definitionCN: 让外部进入的通俗说法；含义更宽泛，也可涵盖投资、文化与信息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective inside the phrase meant 'of a free man', so liberalizing trade is treating exchange as something not chained.
normal.cn: 短语中的形容词本义是「自由人的」，因此放开贸易就是把交换当成不被锁住的事。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberalize, liberalized, liberalization, liberality and liberty.
normal.cn: 同族词包括开放的、使自由化、已放开的、自由化、开明与自由。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the negotiating sense: talks, a round, multilateral and unilateral.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出谈判义：谈判、一轮、多边与单边。

normal.en: The opposite phrase is protectionism, and the two are constantly weighed against each other.
normal.cn: 反面的说法是保护主义，两者常被拿来互相权衡。

normal.en: The old sense of trade is a track or a course, which is why trade is something that runs along a route.
normal.cn: trade 的旧义是路径或走向，所以贸易被想成沿某条路线运行的事。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate at a border, then the lock being taken off and the gate pushed open.
abstract.cn: 想象边境上一道锁着的门，锁被取下，门被推开。

abstract.en: Picture a long list of charges at a customs desk, each line struck through with a pen.
abstract.cn: 想象海关柜台上的一长串收费条目，被笔一行行划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a knot loosening strand by strand until the rope lies straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被一根根松开，直到绳子完全伸直。

examples.en: Trade liberalization brought cheaper parts but also factory closures.
examples.cn: 贸易自由化带来了更便宜的零部件，也带来了工厂关停。

examples.en: The report urged faster trade liberalization in services.
examples.cn: 该报告呼吁在服务领域加快贸易自由化。

examples.en: Farm lobbies resisted further trade liberalization on grain.
examples.cn: 农业游说团体抵制在谷物上进一步贸易自由化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贸易 + 使自由」——把跨境买卖的锁一道道解开 → 贸易自由化

root: trade 出自中古低地德语，本义「路径、走向」，十六世纪起指货物交换；liberal 出自拉丁 liberalis「自由人的、慷慨的」，源头 liber「自由的」，更深来源不确定；抽象后缀经法语出自拉丁与希腊。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loosening: a duty comes off, then the licence rules, then a whole negotiating round, then a country acts alone, then services and investors are let in, then the price of adjustment is paid, then the statistic moves, and finally any exchange is freed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个松开动作展开：先是关税取下，再是许可证规则，接着是一整轮谈判，然后一国单做，服务与投资者被放进来，调整的代价被付清，统计数字随之变动，最后任何交换都被解开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a customs gate lifted, a page of duty lines struck through.
core.cn: 核心意象：海关闸杆抬起，一整页税目被划掉。

branches.en: PRICE AND PERMISSION: first the charge is cut, then the paperwork that also stops goods is cut away.
branches.cn: 价钱与许可：先削掉收费，再削掉同样能挡住货物的那叠文件。

branches.en: BARGAINED OR ALONE: the same opening can be traded with partners round a table or done by one government first.
branches.cn: 换来或单做：同一种开放，既可在桌边与伙伴交换，也可由一国政府先行做出。

branches.en: BEYOND GOODS: a foreign bank and a foreign investor meet the same entry barrier as a crate does.
branches.cn: 货物之外：一家外国银行与一位外国投资者，面对的进入壁垒与一只货箱相同。

branches.en: COST AND COUNT: the losers are compensated, and the effect is then read off in trade statistics.
branches.cn: 代价与计数：受损者得到补偿，效果则从贸易统计里读出来。

branches.en: GENERAL FREEDOM: the tariff disappears and only the loosening of a restriction is left.
branches.cn: 一般意义上的放开：关税消失，只剩下限制被松开这件事。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Germanic commercial noun, a Latin adjective of freedom and a borrowed noun suffix, so each part can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语把日耳曼语系的商业名词、表示自由的拉丁形容词与一个借入的名词后缀合在一起，各部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin liber and liberalis supply liberty, liberal, liberality and liberate; the suffix chain from Greek through Latin and French supplies the abstract noun ending in -ization.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liber 与 liberalis 衍生出自由、开放的、开明与解放；从希腊语经拉丁语与法语传下的后缀链，则提供表示「过程」的抽象名词。

items.structure: trade (English noun, from Middle Low German)
items.example: The noun first named a path, then the goods moving along it.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指道路，后指沿路流动的货物。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a person not bound.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「人不受束缚」的意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun of freedom into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「自由」这一名词变成形容词。

items.example: The adjective first described the giving of a free man.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词最初描述自由人的给予。

items.example: The government liberalized the grain trade.

items.structure: -ization (noun suffix, through French from Latin and Greek)
items.example: The suffix names the process rather than the act of one day.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指过程，而非某一天的一次行动。

items.example: Liberalization of the phone market cut prices.
items.exampleCN: 电话市场的放开压低了价格。

items.example: The word is used of people and places, not of tariffs.
items.exampleCN: 这个词用于人与地方，不用于关税。

latinEntries.structure: liber, libera, liberum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 气溶胶；喷雾器；悬浮微粒
definition_en: a suspension of tiny particles in gas, or a pressurized container that sprays such a mist
core_image: 按下喷罐的喷头，细雾在光柱里悬浮不散
scene: 喷油罐一按，细雾在夕阳光柱里亮成一片。 The painter wore a mask against the aerosol of lacquer.
sceneCN: 这里 aerosol 是「喷雾；悬浮微粒」（第 1 个义项：悬浮在气体中的细小颗粒）；句意为喷漆工戴着口罩抵御漆雾。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 aerosolize 加 -ed 构成，义为「雾化了的」
由本词加动词尾 -ize 构成，义为「使成气溶胶；雾化」
由 aerosolize 派生，义为「雾化过程」

senses.title: Particles suspended in gas
senses.definition: a mixture of fine solid particles or liquid droplets suspended in air or another gas
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮在空气或其他气体中的细小固体颗粒或液滴
senses.example: The painter wore a mask against the aerosol of lacquer.
senses.exampleCN: 喷漆工戴着口罩抵御漆雾。
senses.why: Greek aer, 'air', plus sol from 'solution', names literally a solution floating in air.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer（空气）加 sol（溶液），字面就是「悬浮在空气中的溶液」。

senses.title: Pressurized spray container
senses.definition: a metal container that uses gas pressure to release a fine spray
senses.definitionCN: 靠气压喷出细雾的金属罐
senses.example: Shake the aerosol well before spraying the paint.
senses.exampleCN: 喷漆前先把喷雾罐摇匀。
senses.why: The physics term extended by metonymy to the everyday can that makes the mist.
senses.whyCN: 物理名词经转喻扩展到制造雾气的日常罐子。

senses.title: Airborne disease transmission
senses.definition: tiny exhaled droplets that linger in air and can carry pathogens
senses.definitionCN: 呼出后长时间悬浮在空气中、可能携带病原体的微滴
senses.example: Ventilation reduces the risk from infectious aerosols.
senses.exampleCN: 通风能降低传染性气溶胶带来的风险。
senses.why: The same floating-particle image applies to droplets that stay airborne.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「悬浮颗粒」意象被用于久悬不落的飞沫。

intro.en: Aerosol joins Greek aer, 'air', with sol from solution, coined for colloid chemistry in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: aerosol 由希腊语 aer（空气）与 solution 的 sol 拼合，是二十世纪胶体化学的造词。

items.en: The root *wer- underlies the air word aer.
items.cn: 「空气」词 aer 背后是词根 *wer-。

items.en: Aer meant 'air, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」。

items.en: Solution and sol were standard chemistry terms for dispersed systems.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语中 solution 与 sol 已是表示分散系统的标准化学词。

items.en: Aerosol was coined around 1920 for colloidal particles in gas.
items.cn: 约 1920 年，aerosol 被造出，指气体中的胶体颗粒。

items.en: The word now covers spray cans, pollution science and virus research.
items.cn: 如今该词覆盖喷雾罐、污染科学与病毒研究。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same air root; the second gathers related suspension words.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「空气」词根的词；第二组收其他悬浮物相关词。

entries.definition: To introduce air; shares the Greek aer root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「充气；通气」；同享希腊语 aer 词根。

entries.definition: Of the air or an antenna; same aer root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「空中的；天线」；同根 aer。

entries.definition: Requiring oxygen; same aer with bios, 'life'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「需氧的」；同根 aer 加 bios（生命）。

entries.definition: A fine cloud of liquid droplets in air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄雾；水汽」。

entries.definition: Tiny solid particles suspended in air, as in pollution reports.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微粒；颗粒物」，常见于污染报告。

entries.definition: Liquid sent out in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「喷雾；喷洒」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air-plus-solution root and the spray-can scene; the abstract hooks picture floating glitter in a sunbeam.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气加溶液」词根与喷罐场景；抽象记忆点想象光柱里漂浮的微尘。

normal.en: Aero- is air; sol is from solution.
normal.cn: aero- 是空气，sol 来自溶液。

normal.en: An aerosol is a solution floating in air.
normal.cn: 气溶胶就是浮在空气里的「溶液」。

normal.en: Aerosol cans use gas pressure to spray.
normal.cn: 喷雾罐靠气压喷出雾来。

normal.en: Aerosolize is the verb for turning into mist.
normal.cn: aerosolize 是「使雾化」的动词。

normal.en: Virus research studies infectious aerosols.
normal.cn: 病毒研究关注传染性气溶胶。

abstract.en: Picture glitter hanging in a sunbeam.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光柱里悬停的金粉。

abstract.en: Picture a hiss and a fine cold cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象嘶的一声与一团细细的冷雾。

abstract.en: Picture dust motes that never seem to land.
abstract.cn: 想象久久不落的浮尘。

examples.en: The painter wore a mask against the aerosol of lacquer.
examples.cn: 喷漆工戴着口罩抵御漆雾。

examples.en: Aerosol sprays once used ozone-damaging propellants.
examples.cn: 气雾喷剂曾使用破坏臭氧层的推进剂。

examples.en: Scientists measured aerosols from the volcano.
examples.cn: 科学家测量了火山喷出的气溶胶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「air »瘦」——喷罐里的空气一按就「瘦」成细细的雾喷出来。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）+ solution 的 sol（胶体溶液）→ 英语 aerosol（约 1920，胶体化学造词）；核心义是「浮在空气中的细小溶液颗粒」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from suspended particles in gas, to the spray can itself, to airborne droplets in medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从气体中的悬浮微粒，到喷雾罐本身，再到医学上的空气传播飞沫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine mist hanging in a beam of light
core.cn: 核心意象：悬在光柱里不落的细雾

branches.en: Particles too light to fall.
branches.cn: 轻得落不下来的微粒。

branches.en: The can that makes the mist.
branches.cn: 制造雾气的那个罐子。

branches.en: Droplets that carry infection.
branches.cn: 携带传染物的飞沫。

branches.en: Both senses are matter riding the air.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是搭空气便车的物质。

branches.en: Household products use this meaning.
branches.cn: 日用品用的是这个义项。

intro.en: The word joins the Greek air root aero- with the colloid term sol, and the family gives aerosolize and aerosolized.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语「空气」词根 aero- 与胶体术语 sol 组成，同族词有 aerosolize 与 aerosolized。

latinIntro.en: The aero- half is Greek; sol is a modern chemistry coinage from Latin solvere.
latinIntro.cn: aero- 一半来自希腊语；sol 是由拉丁语 solvere（溶解）造的现代化学词。

definition_zh: 起源；派生；推导；词源
definition_en: the process or fact of coming from a source, or the act of obtaining one thing from another
core_image: 一条支渠从主河分出，渠口清楚标着它从哪里来
scene: 这里指「起源」。 The derivation of the formula from two simple laws impressed the class.
sceneCN: 这里 derivation 是「推导」（第 3 个义项：由前提一步步得出结果）；句意：这个公式由两条简单定律推导出来，让全班印象深刻。图中可辨识物件：黑板上的公式、两条起始定律、箭头、学生笔记。

senses.title: The fact of coming from a source
senses.titleCN: 来源：这东西是从哪儿来的
senses.definition: the origin or source from which something comes
senses.definitionCN: 某物所来自的起源或源头
senses.example: The derivation of the family name is still disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个姓氏的来源仍有争议。
senses.why: derivare means 'to lead water off a stream'. Derivation names the traceable route from a source to the thing that now exists.
senses.whyCN: derivare 意为“从溪流引水”。derivation 命名的是从源头到现存事物之间可追踪的路径。

senses.title: Word formation by affixes
senses.titleCN: 构词派生：给词根加零件
senses.definition: in linguistics, the formation of a new word from an existing word or root by adding affixes
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上通过加词缀从既有词或词根形成新词
senses.example: The derivation of 'unhelpful' uses the prefix un- and the suffix -ful.
senses.exampleCN: unhelpful 的派生用了前缀 un- 和后缀 -ful。
senses.why: A root is the main stream; a prefix or suffix is the branch canal. Derivation is the operation that opens the new channel and changes the word's meaning or class.
senses.whyCN: 词根是主溪流；前缀或后缀是支渠。derivation 就是开出新水道、并改变词义或词性的操作。

senses.title: Step-by-step mathematical proof
senses.definition: the process of reaching a result by a series of logical or mathematical steps
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列逻辑或数学步骤得出结果的过程
senses.example: The derivation takes only three lines but requires a careful assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 这个推导只有三行，但需要一个谨慎的假设。
senses.why: Each step follows from the one before, like water running down a channel. The result is not invented; it is led out from the starting premises.
senses.whyCN: 每一步都从前一步流出，像水沿水道下行。结果不是凭空发明，而是从起始前提引出。

senses.title: Making one compound from another
senses.titleCN: 化学衍生：从旧物质造新物质
senses.definition: the chemical process or relationship by which one substance is obtained from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种物质得到另一种物质的化学过程或关系
senses.example: The derivation of the dye from coal tar was a 19th-century advance.
senses.exampleCN: 从煤焦油制取这种染料是 19 世纪的进步。
senses.why: The original compound keeps its skeleton while a group is changed, so the new substance is a channel led off the old material.
senses.whyCN: 原化合物保留骨架、只改一个基团，因此新物质是从旧材料引出的水道。

senses.title: The study of where a word came from
senses.definition: the etymological history of a particular word, including the forms it passed through
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定词的历史来源，包括它经历的各个形式
senses.example: The dictionary entry gives the derivation of 'salary' from Latin sal.
senses.exampleCN: 词典条目给出了 salary 源自拉丁语 sal 的词源。
senses.why: Etymological derivation is sense 1 applied to words: the modern form is water led from an older stream, and the dictionary maps the route.
senses.whyCN: 词源是第 1 义用在词上：现代形式是从更古老溪流引出的水，词典画出这条路线。

senses.title: Logical inference
senses.definition: the drawing of a conclusion from premises by reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 通过推理从前提得出结论
senses.example: The derivation of her guilt from those facts is not convincing.
senses.exampleCN: 从那些事实推出她有罪的推论并不令人信服。
senses.why: Logic treats a conclusion as something obtained from premises rather than asserted on its own, so the water metaphor extends to reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把结论看成从前提获得的东西，而不是自行断言，于是引水隐喻扩展到推理。

senses.title: Diverting a watercourse
senses.definition: the physical act of leading water from its natural course to another channel
senses.definitionCN: 把水从其自然水道引到另一条水道的实际动作
senses.example: The derivation of the stream for irrigation began in the 18th century.
senses.exampleCN: 为灌溉引走这条溪水始于 18 世纪。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of derivare and the source of all the others. Engineering makes the metaphor visible: the new channel is cut and the water follows.
senses.whyCN: 这是 derivare 的字面义，也是其他义项的源头。工程让隐喻变得可见：新渠一开，水就跟着走。

senses.title: Origin of authority or meaning
senses.titleCN: 来源：权力或意义从何处取得
senses.definition: the source from which a right, power or meaning is understood to come
senses.definitionCN: 某项权利、权力或意义被认为所来自的源头
senses.example: The court examined the derivation of the agency's authority.
senses.exampleCN: 法院审查了该机构权力的来源。
senses.why: Rights and meanings are also treated as flowing from a source. The noun asks where the water comes from, not whether it is wet.
senses.whyCN: 权利和意义也被当成从某源头流出。这个名词问的是水从哪里来，而不是水是否湿。

intro.en: Derivation goes back to Latin derivatio, from derivare 'to lead water off', de- 'from' plus rivus 'stream'. The word moved from irrigation to language, logic and chemistry without changing its shape.
intro.cn: derivation 可追到拉丁 derivatio，来自 derivare“引走水”，由 de-“从”和 rivus“溪流”构成。这个词从灌溉转到语言、逻辑和化学，形态始终未变。

items.en: rivus 'stream' gives the image of a channel with a direction. The same root produces rivalis 'one who shares a stream', hence English rival.
items.cn: rivus“溪流”提供了有方向的水道意象。同一词根产生 rivalis“共用溪流者”，即英语 rival。

items.en: derivare 'to lead off water' describes an engineering act: cutting a branch canal so that part of the flow takes a new route.
items.cn: derivare“引走水”描述一个工程动作：开一条支渠，让部分水流改走新路线。

items.en: derivatio named the act of diverting water and, figuratively, the tracing of something to its source. The figurative use is already present in Latin.
items.cn: derivatio 命名引水动作，并比喻指把某物追溯到其源头。比喻用法在拉丁语中已经存在。

items.en: English adopts derivation in the 15th century for origin and descent. The exact earliest record is uncertain because derive and derivation entered through French forms.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪采用 derivation 表示起源与传承。由于 derive 与 derivation 是经法语形式进入的，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: In the 19th century, linguistics fixed derivation as the formation of words by affixation, separating it from inflection, which only changes grammatical form.
items.cn: 19 世纪，语言学把 derivation 固定为通过加词缀构词的过程，并与只改变语法形式的屈折区分开。

items.en: Mathematics and chemistry adopted the noun for stepwise proofs and for making one compound from another. Both keep the idea of a traceable route from a source.
items.cn: 数学与化学采用这个名词表示逐步证明和从一种化合物制取另一种。两者都保留了“从源头可追踪的路径”这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deriv- stem with different suffixes; the near-meaning group separates origin, formation, proof and etymology.
note.cn: 形近组共享 deriv- 词干、后缀不同；近义组区分起源、构词、证明与词源。

entries.definition: a thing produced from another source. Derivation is the process; derivative is the product.
entries.definitionCN: 从另一来源产生的事物。derivation 是过程，derivative 是产物。

entries.definition: to obtain or originate from a source; the verb names the action behind the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从某来源获得或起源；这个动词命名过程名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: relating to derivation, especially in word formation; it describes the mechanism, not the history.
entries.definitionCN: 与派生有关的，尤指构词；它描述机制，而不是历史。

entries.definition: the point where something begins; derivation adds the sense of a trackable route from that point.
entries.definitionCN: 某物开始的点；derivation 另含“从该点可追踪的路径”之意。

entries.definition: the study of word origins; a derivation is the specific history of one word, while etymology is the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 词源学；derivation 是一个词的具体来源史，而 etymology 是学科。

entries.definition: a complete argument showing a result follows from premises; a derivation is the step sequence itself.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某结果由前提推出的完整论证；derivation 是那串步骤本身。

entries.definition: the process of being formed; it is broader than derivation and does not require an identifiable source.
entries.definitionCN: 形成的过程；比 derivation 更宽，不要求可识别的源头。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'from' + rivus 'stream': derivation traces the branch back to the stream.
normal.cn: de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”：derivation 把支渠一路追溯回溪流。

normal.en: In linguistics, remember the pair derivation and inflection: one makes a new word, the other changes a form.
normal.cn: 语言学里记住 derivation 与 inflection 这对词：一个造新词，一个改形式。

normal.en: A mathematical derivation is written step by step, so each line is a drop of water moving down the channel.
normal.cn: 数学推导是一行一行写的，每一行都是水道里向下流动的一滴水。

normal.en: The phrase word derivation points straight at etymology, the history of a form.
normal.cn: 短语 word derivation 直接指向词源，也就是一个形式的来路。

normal.en: derive, derivation, derivative and derivational share rivus, so the family can be learned as one water system.
normal.cn: derive、derivation、derivative、derivational 共享 rivus，可以把这个词族当成一套水系来学。

abstract.en: Think of a hand-drawn map where a dotted trail leads from a source to a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手绘地图，一条虚线从源头一路引到村庄。

abstract.en: Think of a genealogy chart: each name is connected by a line to the ancestor it came from.
abstract.cn: 想象一张族谱：每个名字都用一条线连到它的祖先。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe that starts with one dough and produces three different breads.
abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱：同一团面做出三种不同的面包。

examples.en: The derivation of the word 'money' goes back to a temple of Juno.
examples.cn: money 这个词的词源可追到一座朱诺神庙。

examples.en: She published a full derivation of the equation in the appendix.
examples.cn: 她在附录中发表了该方程的完整推导。

examples.en: The derivation of the new plastic from plant oil reduced costs.
examples.cn: 从植物油制取这种新塑料降低了成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地riveration”——地（de）上的 river（河）引出一条支流，一路追溯到源头 → derivation 起源、推导、词源

root: 拉丁 derivare“从溪流引水”（de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”）；derivat- 词干 + -ion 过程名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one path: a traceable route from a source to a result, whether the source is a stream, a root, a premise or a parent compound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一条路径：从源头到结果的可追踪路线——源头可以是溪流、词根、前提或母体化合物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch canal cut from a main river, with its intake clearly marked.
core.cn: 核心意象：从主河开出的支渠，取水口标得清清楚楚。

branches.en: WORD ORIGIN: the history of a particular word, through the forms it has taken.
branches.cn: 词源：一个特定词的历史来源，包括它经历的各个形式。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AND CHEMISTRY: affixation opens a new word channel, and chemical change opens a new compound channel.
branches.cn: 语言与化学：加词缀开出新词水道，化学变化开出新化合物水道。

branches.en: PROOF AND INFERENCE: a mathematical derivation and a logical inference both move step by step from premises to a result.
branches.cn: 证明与推论：数学推导与逻辑推论都从前提一步步走向结果。

branches.en: WATER AND AUTHORITY: diverting a stream and deriving a right from a source are literal and institutional versions of the same intake.
branches.cn: 水与权力：引溪水与从源头取得权利，是同一取水口的字面版与制度版。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: all extensions ask the same question, 'where did this come from and by what route?'.
branches.cn: 基础义：所有引申都在问同一个问题——“它从哪里来，沿哪条路线来？”

intro.en: Derivation is derivat- plus -ion. Latin de- and rivus are fused; English uses -ion, -ive, -ational and -able as the productive endings of this family.
intro.cn: derivation 是 derivat- 加 -ion。拉丁 de- 与 rivus 已融合；英语用 -ion、-ive、-ational、-able 作为这个词族的能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' gives rivulus, derivare and derivatio. English relatives include river, rival, derive, derivative and derivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus“溪流”派生 rivulus、derivare、derivatio。英语同族词包括 river、rival、derive、derivative、derivation。

items.meaningCN: 从某来源获得；派生（de-“从”+ rivare“开渠引水”）
items.example: The formula derives from a simple observation.
items.exampleCN: 这个公式来自一个简单观察。

items.meaningCN: 推导；派生；来源（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The derivation of the name took two pages.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字的来源考据写了两页。

items.meaningCN: 派生的；衍生物（-ive 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: The derivative compound is easier to store.
items.exampleCN: 这种衍生物更容易储存。

items.meaningCN: 与派生有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: Derivational morphology studies how new words are built.
items.exampleCN: 派生形态学研究新词如何构成。

items.example: The conclusion is derivable from the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个结论可以从数据推导出来。

items.example: The river bends west before reaching the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在入海前向西转弯。

items.meaningCN: 竞争对手（同源词，原指共用溪流者）
items.example: The two ports are rivals for the same trade.
items.exampleCN: 这两个港口是同一贸易的竞争对手。

items.meaningCN: 源自（固定搭配，介词 from 标记源头）
items.example: The custom derives from an old harvest festival.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗源自一个古老的丰收节。

latinEntries.meaning: a diverting; a tracing to a source

definition_zh: 诡计；巧计；（人工的）技巧
definition_en: clever trickery used to deceive, or skillful ingenuity in making things
core_image: 幕后巧手布下的机关与圈套
scene: 谈判桌上他笑容可掬，袖中却捏着一份拟好的附加条款。 The treaty failed because of his artifice.
sceneCN: 这里 artifice 是「诡计」（第 1 个义项：欺骗性的巧计）；句意是因为他的花招，条约告吹。

derivatives.zh: artifice 加 -er，义为「巧匠；技工；（军）工兵」
同根形容词，义为「人工的；虚假的」
art 加 -ful，义为「狡猾的；巧妙的」

senses.title: Clever deception
senses.definition: a cunning trick or scheme designed to deceive others
senses.definitionCN: 旨在欺骗他人的狡猾手段或圈套
senses.example: Her apology was just an artifice to win back his trust.
senses.exampleCN: 她的道歉不过是赢回他信任的伎俩。
senses.why: Ars means skill, so a skill turned toward cheating becomes artifice.
senses.whyCN: ars 意为「技艺」，技艺用于行骗便成了 artifice。

senses.title: Skillful ingenuity in making
senses.definition: ingenious skill in construction or craftsmanship, sometimes admiring
senses.definitionCN: 制作上的精巧技艺，有时含赞赏意味
senses.example: The clock shows the artifice of eighteenth-century makers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座钟显示了十八世纪工匠的巧艺。
senses.why: The original sense of trained skill remains in this neutral use.
senses.whyCN: 「受训技艺」的本义保留在这一中性用法中。

senses.title: Artificial contrivance, lack of naturalness
senses.definition: unnatural cleverness or affectation in manner or expression
senses.definitionCN: 举止或表达中不自然的做作与矫饰
senses.example: She spoke with such artifice that nobody believed her.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话矫揉造作，没人相信她。
senses.why: Made skill contrasts with what is genuine and natural.
senses.whyCN: 人造之巧与真实自然相对照。

intro.en: Artifice comes from Latin artificium, something made with skill, from ars and facere.
intro.cn: artifice 源自拉丁语 artificium（以技艺制成之物），由 ars 与 facere 复合。

items.en: Root *h2er- (to fit together) gives ars, skill; *dheh1- gives facere, to make.
items.cn: 词根 *h2er-（接合）衍生 ars（技艺）；*dheh1- 衍生 facere（制作）（重构形式）。

items.en: Artificium meant a work of skill, craft, or device.
items.cn: 拉丁语 artificium 指技艺之作、工艺或巧器。

items.en: Old French artifice carried both craftsmanship and cunning device.
items.cn: 古法语 artifice 兼指工艺与狡黠机巧。

items.en: The word entered English in the sixteenth century with the trickery sense uppermost.
items.cn: 16 世纪该词进入英语，诡计义已占上风。

items.en: Today it names deception primarily, with neutral craftsmanship senses in older texts.
items.cn: 现代英语以欺骗义为主，中性工艺义多见于早期文本。

note.en: Artifice is the dark twin of art: the same skill, aimed at cheating.
note.cn: artifice 是 art 的暗面孪生：同样的技艺，用于行骗。

entries.definition: made by humans, not natural
entries.definitionCN: 人工的、非天然的，artifice 的同根形容词

entries.definition: a skilled maker or craftsman
entries.definitionCN: 巧匠、技工，artifice 的施动者名词

entries.definition: plural of office
entries.definitionCN: 办公室（复数），词尾拼写相近但词义无关

entries.definition: a trick intended to deceive
entries.definitionCN: 诱敌之计、骗局，与 artifice 的诡计义相近

entries.definition: cunning deceit in behavior
entries.definitionCN: 狡诈，侧重品性中的欺骗倾向

entries.definition: a plan or scheme for gaining an advantage
entries.definitionCN: 计谋、策略，军事色彩较浓

normalIntro.en: See art plus fice (make): skill used to make tricks.
normalIntro.cn: 把词看成 art + fice（制作）：用技艺做圈套。

normal.en: ars (skill) + facere (make) = skill-made device.
normal.cn: ars（技艺）+ facere（制作）＝巧制之器。

normal.en: The dark sense dominates: cunning deception.
normal.cn: 贬义主导：狡猾的欺诈。

normal.en: Same root: artificial, artificer, artisan.
normal.cn: 同根词：artificial、artificer、artisan。

normal.en: Without artifice means honest and natural.
normal.cn: without artifice 即坦率自然。

normal.en: A stratagem is a grander plan; an artifice a smaller trick.
normal.cn: stratagem 是大计，artifice 是小伎俩。

abstract.en: Picture a magician's sleeve hiding the trick card.
abstract.cn: 想象魔术师袖中藏着的戏法牌。

abstract.en: See a smiling face with crossed fingers behind its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一张笑脸背后交叉着手指。

abstract.en: Hear gears clicking inside a false-bottomed box.
abstract.cn: 聆听暗层盒子里的齿轮咔嗒声。

examples.en: The spy's artifice won him access to the files.
examples.cn: 间谍的巧计为他打开了档案室。

examples.en: She won the game by artifice rather than skill.
examples.cn: 她靠诡计而非实力赢了比赛。

examples.en: The film avoids all artifice and simply records daily life.
examples.cn: 这部影片毫无矫饰，只是记录日常生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿提·菲斯」——阿提在费用（fee）报表上耍花招，谎报数目，全靠「阿提菲斯」的伎俩。

root: 拉丁语 ars（技艺）+ facere（制作）→ artificium（巧制之物）→ 古法语 artifice → 英语 artifice；同根词 artificial、artisan、artifact。

sensesIntro.en: From skilled making to cunning deception and artificial manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 由精巧的制作延伸到狡黠的欺骗与做作的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: skilled hands building a hidden trap
core.cn: 核心意象：巧手暗造机关

branches.en: skill aimed at cheating
branches.cn: 用于行骗的技艺

branches.en: craft in its neutral sense
branches.cn: 中性义的工艺

branches.en: unnatural polish of manner
branches.cn: 举止上的不自然雕饰

branches.en: made surfaces versus the real
branches.cn: 人造表面与真实的对照

branches.en: the maker behind the device
branches.cn: 机关背后的制作者

intro.en: The root facere (make) recurs across English words of making.
intro.cn: 词根 facere（制作）反复出现在英语制作用词中。

latinIntro.en: Ars (skill) also gives art, artist, artifact and artisan.
latinIntro.cn: ars（技艺）同时派生出 art、artist、artifact 与 artisan。

definition_zh: adj. 穿着…衣服的；被…覆盖的（常用于复合词）
definition_en: dressed in a particular way, or covered with something
core_image: 矿工们裹着厚厚的工装走下矿井
scene: 矿工们穿着厚重的防护服，走进幽深的矿井。 The miners, clad in heavy suits, entered the dark shaft.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clad 指穿着…衣服的；句意是矿工们穿着厚重的防护服，走进幽深的矿井。

senses.title: Dressed in a particular way
senses.definition: wearing clothes of a stated kind
senses.definitionCN: 穿着某种特定衣物
senses.example: She was clad in black silk from head to foot.
senses.exampleCN: 她从头上到脚下都穿着黑绸。
senses.why: Clad is the old past participle of clothe, used as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: clad 是 clothe 的古老过去分词，用作形容词。

senses.title: Covered with something
senses.definition: covered or coated with a substance
senses.definitionCN: 被某种物质覆盖或包住
senses.example: The hills were clad in fresh snow.
senses.exampleCN: 山丘覆盖着新雪。
senses.why: The sense moved from clothes to any covering.
senses.whyCN: 词义从衣服扩展到任何覆盖物。

intro.en: Clad is an old past form of clothe that became an adjective of covering.
intro.cn: clad 是 clothe 的古老过去式，后来成为表示覆盖的形容词。

items.en: Clathian means to clothe.
items.cn: 古英语 clathian 意为给…穿衣。

items.en: Clad serves as past tense and past participle.
items.cn: 中古英语 clad 作过去式与过去分词。

items.en: Writers use clad before nouns, as in clad in wool.
items.cn: 十六世纪作家把 clad 用在名词前，如 clad in wool。

items.en: Snow-clad and armour-clad become common.
items.cn: 十九世纪 snow-clad、armour-clad 流行。

items.en: Clad survives mainly in formal and poetic prose.
items.cn: 现代 clad 多见于正式与文学语体。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names other ways of being dressed.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组列出穿衣的其他说法。

entries.definition: A lump of earth.
entries.definitionCN: 土块。

entries.definition: Happy about something.
entries.definitionCN: 高兴的。

entries.definition: A device that grips.
entries.definitionCN: 夹具。

entries.definition: Wearing clothes of a kind.
entries.definitionCN: 穿好衣服的。

entries.definition: Wearing clothes; covered.
entries.definitionCN: 穿衣的；覆盖的。

entries.definition: Dressed, often formally.
entries.definitionCN: 盛装的。

normalIntro.en: Clad is what clothe leaves behind: the dressed person.
normalIntro.cn: clad 就是 clothe 留下的结果：穿好衣的人。

normal.en: Clothe turns into clad.
normal.cn: clothe 变成 clad。

normal.en: Clad in white means dressed in white.
normal.cn: clad in white 意为穿白衣。

normal.en: Add a noun to make compounds.
normal.cn: 加名词构成复合词。

normal.en: Snow-clad hills are covered in snow.
normal.cn: snow-clad 的山是被雪覆盖的山。

normal.en: Clad is literary, not everyday casual.
normal.cn: clad 偏文学，不用于日常口语。

abstract.en: Cloth frozen into a description.
abstract.cn: 布料凝固成一个形容词。

abstract.en: A hill wearing a white coat.
abstract.cn: 披着白外套的山。

abstract.en: Dressing that became covering.
abstract.cn: 从穿衣变成覆盖。

examples.en: The dancers were clad in silver and white.
examples.cn: 舞者们穿着银白相间的衣服。

examples.en: He arrived clad only in shorts and sandals.
examples.cn: 他来时只穿短裤和凉鞋。

examples.en: The valley lay clad in morning mist.
examples.cn: 山谷笼罩在晨雾之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: clothe 的过去分词 clad → 被衣服「包住」的状态，即穿着与覆盖。

root: 古英语 clathian（给…穿衣）→ 中古英语 clad（过去式/过去分词）→ 形容词 clad

sensesIntro.en: The same past form describes people in clothes and hills in snow.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个过去式既写穿衣的人，也写覆雪的山。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy coat wrapped round a miner
core.cn: 核心意象：厚外套裹住一名矿工

branches.en: A dancer in silver silk.
branches.cn: 穿银绸的舞者。

branches.en: A traveller in shorts and sandals.
branches.cn: 穿短裤凉鞋的旅人。

branches.en: A hill under fresh snow.
branches.cn: 新雪覆盖的山丘。

branches.en: A valley wrapped in mist.
branches.cn: 晨雾笼罩的山谷。

branches.en: A body wearing something as a layer.
branches.cn: 以某一层包裹身体。

intro.en: Clad belongs to a small family of dressing words; the list adds covering and wearing terms.
intro.cn: clad 属于一小族穿衣词；下面列出覆盖与穿着的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis is a garment and tegere is to cover.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis 意为衣服，tegere 意为覆盖。

latinEntries.exampleCN: vestis 产生 vest 与 invest。
tegere 产生 integument 与 tegument。
clathian 产生 clothe 与 clad。

definition_zh: 预料之中的；（人、车、货）预期到达的；按理应当的；符合预期的；（数学）期望的；（分娩）预产期将至的；预计的（收入、结果）；（角色）被指望接任的
definition_en: regarded as likely to happen or to arrive, and therefore counted on in advance

scene: 果园边的空地上，农户把防霜布一层层铺开，说今年大概又要提前降温。 The first frost came later than anyone had expected.
sceneCN: 这里 expected 指「事先认定会发生、因而据此等待的」（第 1 个义项：预料之中会发生）；句意为初霜来得比任何人预料的都晚。可辨识物件：防霜布、果树、百叶箱、结霜的草叶。

pos.zh: 预料之中的；预期到达的；按理应当的
expect 的过去式与过去分词

derivatives.zh: 期待；预期（尤指期待中的状态）

senses.title: Regarded as likely to happen
senses.definition: believed in advance to be likely, so that people plan and prepare on the strength of that belief
senses.definitionCN: 事先相信某事很可能发生，人们据此安排与准备
senses.example: The first frost came later than anyone had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 初霜来得比任何人预料的都晚。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word means to look out for something, so what is expected is what one has been watching the horizon for.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词意为「向外张望某物」，所以被预料的事，就是一直盯着地平线在等的那件事。

senses.title: Due to arrive at a known time
senses.definition: described of a person, train, parcel or message that is scheduled or reckoned to arrive at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 形容人、列车、包裹或消息按时刻或估算应于某时到达
senses.example: The morning train is expected at platform four within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 早班列车预计十分钟内到达四号站台。
senses.why: Travel and trade needed a word for the thing already on its way, and the looking-out sense turned into a timetable sense.
senses.whyCN: 出行与贸易需要一个词来指已经在路上的东西，于是「向外张望」义就变成了时刻表义。

senses.title: Supposed to, by rule or duty
senses.definition: required or obliged by rule, role or politeness, so that not doing it is a fault rather than a surprise
senses.definitionCN: 因规则、角色或礼节而应当做，不做即为过失，而不只是令人意外
senses.example: Visitors are expected to sign in at the front desk before entering.
senses.exampleCN: 来访者进入前应当在前台登记。
senses.why: Once people reliably look for a behaviour, its absence becomes a breach, and expectation turns into obligation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们稳定地期待某种行为，它的缺席就成了失礼，期待也就变成了义务。

senses.title: Matching what was forecast
senses.definition: described of a result or figure that lands where the forecast said it would, neither above nor below
senses.definitionCN: 形容结果或数字正落在预测的位置，不高也不低
senses.example: Sales were as expected, so the board kept the original plan.
senses.exampleCN: 销售正如预期，因此董事会维持原计划。
senses.why: This sense compares two things at once: the forecast in the mind and the number in the report.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项同时比较两样东西：心里的预测，与报告里的那个数字。

senses.title: The average outcome of a random trial
senses.definition: in probability, the long-run average value of a variable, obtained by weighting each outcome by its chance
senses.definitionCN: 在概率论中，指变量在大量重复试验下的平均值，按各结果发生的概率加权
senses.example: The expected number of defective parts per batch is two.
senses.exampleCN: 每批零件中不合格件数的期望值是两个。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the forecast image but made it exact: what one expects over many trials is the weighted mean.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了这个「预先估计」的图景，却把它精确化：在大量试验里所预期的，就是加权平均。

senses.title: The date a baby is due
senses.definition: the estimated date on which a birth is calculated to occur, used in medicine for planning care
senses.definitionCN: 按估算算出的分娩日期，医学上用于安排照护
senses.example: Her expected date of delivery falls in the first week of March.
senses.exampleCN: 她的预产期在三月的第一周。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word because a due date is a forecast that a whole ward plans around.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用这个词，因为预产期是整个病区都要据此安排的一个预测。

senses.title: Estimated income or result
senses.definition: in finance and planning, describing earnings, costs or returns worked out in advance from current evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在金融与规划中指依据现有证据事先算出的收益、成本或回报
senses.example: Expected revenue for the quarter was revised upward after the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 合同签订后，本季的预计收入被上调。
senses.why: Budgets run on numbers that do not exist yet, and the word marks them as estimates rather than records.
senses.whyCN: 预算靠的是尚不存在的数字，这个词把这些数字标为估算，而非既成记录。

senses.title: The role one is counted on to take
senses.definition: described of a person marked out by others to succeed, inherit or represent them, whether or not they agree
senses.definitionCN: 形容被他人指定去接任、继承或代表的人，无论本人是否同意
senses.example: He was the expected successor, and the whole office knew it before he did.
senses.exampleCN: 他是众望所归的继任者，全办公室都比他自己更早知道。
senses.why: The word can shift from an event to a person: the one everyone looks towards is the one expected to step in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从事件转到人身上：所有人都在望向的那个人，就是被指望接手的那个。

intro.en: Expected is the past participle of expect, from Latin exspectare 'to look out for, await', which joins ex- 'out' to spectare 'to look at'. Spectare is itself a frequentative of specere 'to see', so the whole word pictures someone watching outward for what is coming.
intro.cn: expected 是 expect 的过去分词，源自拉丁 exspectare「向外张望、等待」，由 ex-「向外」加 spectare「看」构成。spectare 又是 specere「看见」的反复形式，因此整个词构出的图景是一个人朝外盯着即将到来的东西。

items.en: Specere meant 'to see, look'. It supplies the looking in aspect, where ad- means towards, in inspect, where in- means into, in respect, where re- means back, and in suspect, where sub- means from below; spectacle and species take noun endings instead. Each word differs in prefix and in sense, so they are relatives and not synonyms.
items.cn: specere 意为「看见、看」。aspect 用 ad-「朝向」，inspect 用 in-「向内」，respect 用 re-「回」，suspect 用 sub-「从下」；spectacle 与 species 则改用名词词尾。每个词的前缀与词义都不同，因此它们是同源词而非同义词。

items.en: Spectare was the frequentative of specere, meaning to look at again and again, to watch; the ending adds repeated or sustained action rather than a single glance.
items.cn: spectare 是 specere 的反复形式，意为「一再地看、观看」；这个词尾添加的是反复或持续的动作，而不是看一眼。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus spectare gave exspectare, to look out for, to watch for someone's coming, and so to await or anticipate.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 spectare 构成 exspectare，意为「向外张望、留意某人的到来」，由此引申为等待与预料。

items.en: Its past participle exspectatus meant awaited or looked-for; that participle is the shape English later borrowed and turned into a standalone adjective.
items.cn: 它的过去分词意为「被等待的、被盼望的」；英语后来借入的正是这个分词形式，并把它变成独立的形容词。

items.en: English used the participle inside the verb phrase first, then allowed it to stand before a noun as an adjective; the probability sense of expected value is a much later technical coinage.
items.cn: 英语最早把这个分词用在动词短语里，后来才允许它直接放在名词前作形容词；期望值这一概率义则是晚得多的技术性用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of specere is a reconstruction, not a recorded form, and the first use of the participle as an attributive adjective cannot be dated to a single year.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：specere 在拉丁语之前的形式属重构而非有记录的形式；这个分词首次用作定语形容词的年代也无法确定到某一年。

note.en: Group one holds words that all descend from the Latin verb for seeing, and every one of them must be told apart by its prefix; none is a false friend, but none can replace another. Group two holds words of foreknowledge that differ in whether they are based on evidence, schedule, duty or mere likelihood.
note.cn: 第一组都出自拉丁语中表示「看」的动词，每一个都要按前缀分辨；它们没有假同源词，但也都不能互相替换。第二组是表示「预先知道」的词，区别在于依据的是证据、时刻表、义务，还是仅仅可能。

entries.definition: The verb from which the participle comes: to look out for something and so to think it likely; the adjective describes the result of that looking.
entries.definitionCN: 这个分词所来自的动词：向外留意某事，因而认为它很可能；形容词描述的就是这番留意之后的状态。

entries.definition: The noun names the mental picture of what is coming, or the standard others hold you to; expected describes the thing that matches such a picture.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词指心中对将来之事的图景，或他人对你的标准；expected 则形容符合这幅图景的事物。

entries.definition: Describing the person who is waiting, often with hope, as in an expectant mother; it points at the watcher, not at the event.
entries.definitionCN: 形容正在等待、常带盼望的人，如待产的孕妇；它指向的是等待者，而不是那个事件。

entries.definition: The direct negation: what was not looked for and therefore has no plan attached to it.
entries.definitionCN: 直接否定形式：指未曾被留意、因而也没有任何预案的东西。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus the seeing root: to look closely into something in order to judge it; the prefix turns outward waiting into inward examination.
entries.definitionCN: in-「向内」加「看」的词根：为了评判而仔细查看某物；这个前缀把向外的等待变成向内的检查。

entries.definition: From the same looking root, naming something put before the eyes; it needs no expectation and no future.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这个「看」的词根，指摆在眼前供人观看之物；它既不需要预期，也不指向未来。

entries.definition: Expected and usually acted upon in advance, as when supplies are ordered before the rush; it implies preparation, where expected may be passive.
entries.definitionCN: 不仅预料，而且通常提前采取行动，如在高峰前订好货；它含准备之意，而 expected 可以只是被动地等着。

entries.definition: Stated in advance on the strength of data, a model or a pattern; it claims a method behind the forecast, which expected does not.
entries.definitionCN: 依据数据、模型或规律事先说出；它声称预测背后有方法，而 expected 不作此声称。

entries.definition: Owed or scheduled to happen at a set time, as a train or a payment; it fixes the time, while expected only fixes the likelihood.
entries.definitionCN: 应在某一固定时刻发生或应付，如列车或款项；它锁定时间，而 expected 只锁定可能性。

entries.definition: Required by duty or accepted as true on hearsay; it carries a hint of doubt or reproach that expected usually lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 因义务而应当，或因传闻而被认为如此；它带一点怀疑或责备，而 expected 通常没有这层意味。

entries.tag: looking forward to a future role
entries.definition: Describing someone or something likely to become relevant in the future, as a prospective buyer; it points at a future state, not at a forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 形容将来可能变得相关的人或物，如意向买家；它指向未来的状态，而不是一份预测。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real family of seeing words with their different prefixes, the real phrases, and the technical uses in probability and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语素、真实的「看」词族及其不同前缀、真实的固定搭配，以及概率与医学中的专业用法。

normal.en: The prefix means out and the root means look, so to expect is to keep looking out for what is coming.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向外」，词根意为「看」，所以预料就是一直朝外盯着将要到来的东西。

normal.en: The root of seeing also gives aspect, inspect, respect, suspect, spectacle and species, each with a different prefix or ending.
normal.cn: 这个「看」的词根还生出 aspect、inspect、respect、suspect、spectacle 与 species，各自带不同的前缀或词尾。

normal.en: The participle became an adjective: expected arrival, expected result, expected value, expected date of delivery.
normal.cn: 这个分词变成了形容词：预期到达、预期结果、期望值、预产期。

normal.en: The family runs expect, expects, expecting, expectation, expectations, expectancy and unexpected.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 expect、expects、expecting、expectation、expectations、expectancy 与 unexpected。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the frame: as expected, than expected, be expected to, meet expectations.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出框架：正如预料、比预想的、预计会、达到预期。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cupped above the eyes, shading them, though there is nothing on the road yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手搭在眼睛上方遮光，尽管路上还什么都没有。

abstract.en: Picture a chair already pulled out at a table for a guest who has not rung the bell.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌旁已经为一位还没按门铃的客人拉出了一把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a row of identical envelopes, and the one on top already opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一排一模一样的信封，最上面那封已经被拆开了。

examples.en: The storm was expected to reach the coast before dawn, so the ferries stopped running.
examples.cn: 预计风暴会在天亮前抵达海岸，因此渡轮停航了。

examples.en: Her results were better than expected, which changed the whole timetable.
examples.cn: 她的成绩比预期好，这改变了整个时间安排。

examples.en: In a fair die the expected value of a single roll is three and a half.
examples.cn: 在公平的骰子上，单次投掷的期望值是三点五。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外 + 看」——一直朝外张望，就是在等那件认定会发生的事，也就是预料

root: 拉丁 exspectare「向外张望、等待」= ex-（向外）+ spectare「看」（specere「看见」的反复形式）；expected 是 expect 的过去分词作形容词。同根的 aspect、inspect、respect、suspect、spectacle、species 均出 specere，但前缀与语义不同；specere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: someone looks outward for what is coming. The looking may settle on an event, on an arrival, on a duty, on a forecast that comes true, on an average across many trials, on a birth date, on projected income, or on the person marked to take over.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个人朝外张望将要到来的东西。这番张望可以落在一件事、一次到达、一项应尽之责、一个应验的预测、大量试验的平均值、一个分娩日期、一笔预计收入，或那个被指定接手的人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes fixed on the road, waiting for something already believed to be on its way.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛盯着路，等一件已经相信正在路上的东西。

branches.en: WAITING AND ARRIVING: the same outward look covers a likely event and a vehicle already on its way.
branches.cn: 等待与到达：同一次向外张望，既覆盖很可能发生的事，也覆盖已经在路上的车。

branches.en: DUTY AND SCORE: expectation hardens into a required step, and softens into a number that merely matches the forecast.
branches.cn: 义务与分数：期待硬化成必须执行的一步，也软化成仅仅吻合预测的数字。

branches.en: THE LONG RUN: probability keeps the forecast image but makes it a weighted average over many trials.
branches.cn: 长期重复：概率论保留预测的图景，却把它变成大量试验的加权平均。

branches.en: THE DUE DATE: medicine turns the forecast into a date a whole ward plans around.
branches.cn: 预产日期：医学把预测变成一个整个病区都要据此安排的日期。

branches.en: PROJECTED AND ASSIGNED: what is expected can be a figure in a budget or a person marked for a role.
branches.cn: 预计与被指定：被预期的可以是一份预算里的数字，也可以是一个被指定角色的人。

intro.en: Expected is a Latin participle used as an English adjective; its prefix, its seeing root and its adjective ending all recur across a large family of English words.
intro.cn: expected 是一个用作英语形容词的拉丁分词；它的前缀、表示「看」的词根与形容词词尾，都在英语的一大词族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere gives the act of seeing, spectare gives sustained watching, ex- sends the gaze outward, and the participle ending -tus makes the result into a description.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 specere 提供「看见」的动作，spectare 提供持续的观看，ex- 把目光送向外面，分词词尾 -tus 则把结果变成一种描述。

items.example: The prefix sends the gaze away from the watcher and towards the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把目光从观看者身上送开，投向地平线。

items.example: The root supplies the eye in the image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供了这个词背后图景中的那只眼睛。

items.example: The frequentative form turns a glance into sustained watching.
items.exampleCN: 这个反复形式把一眼变成持续的观看。

items.meaning: to look out for; to await
items.example: The verb names the act of watching the road for someone.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指守着路等某人的动作。

items.meaningCN: 被等待的；被认为会来的
items.example: The first frost came later than anyone had expected.
items.exampleCN: 初霜来得比任何人预料的都晚。

items.meaning: the act or state of awaiting
items.exampleCN: 结果超出了所有人的预期。

items.example: An expectant crowd gathered at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 一群满怀期待的人聚集在门口。

items.example: An unexpected delay ruined the schedule.
items.exampleCN: 一次意外的延误毁了整个日程。

latinEntries.structure: spectare, spectavi, spectatum (verb, first conjugation, frequentative)

definition_zh: 因果的；原因的；表示原因的；因果关系的
definition_en: relating to a cause, or expressing a cause-and-effect relation
core_image: 一根箭头从 A 指向 B：箭头本身不是原因，却标出“谁推了谁”
scene: 研究方法课上，老师在白板上画了一个箭头，从「吸烟」指向「肺癌」。 In the methods class, the teacher draws an arrow from smoking to lung cancer and labels it a causal link.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 causal 是「因果的、因果关系的」（第 1、3 个义项：与原因有关与因果联系）；句意：老师从吸烟画箭头指向肺癌，并把它标为因果关系。图中可辨识物件：白板、箭头、两个方框、马克笔。

pos.zh: 因果的；原因的；表示原因的

senses.title: Relating to a cause
senses.definition: connected with the idea of a cause or with causes in general
senses.definitionCN: 与原因这一概念或一般意义上的原因有关
senses.example: The chapter discusses causal language in ordinary speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章讨论日常言语中的因果语言。
senses.why: Late Latin causalis was simply 'of a cause', formed from causa with -alis. The adjective begins as a label for anything belonging to the category of cause.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 causalis 就是“原因的”，由 causa 加 -alis 构成。这个形容词起初只是给任何属于“原因”范畴的东西贴标签。

senses.title: Expressing cause in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, describing a clause or conjunction that introduces a reason
senses.definitionCN: 语法中描述引出原因的从句或连词
senses.example: Because and since are causal conjunctions.
senses.exampleCN: because 与 since 是表示原因的连词。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the adjective for forms whose whole job is to state a reason. A causal clause does not describe a relation; it performs one in language.
senses.whyCN: 语法借这个形容词来指那些专职陈述理由的形式。原因状语从句不描述一种关系，它在语言中执行一种关系。

senses.title: Marking a cause-effect link
senses.definition: describing a connection in which one thing is held to produce another
senses.definitionCN: 描述一物被认为产生另一物的连接
senses.example: Researchers found a causal link between sleep loss and errors.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者发现睡眠不足与差错之间存在因果联系。
senses.why: This is the most common modern use: the adjective modifies link, relation or connection. It marks the arrow between two boxes.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代用法：形容词修饰 link、relation、connection。它标出两个方框之间的箭头。

senses.title: Causal inference in statistics
senses.definition: in statistics and epidemiology, describing methods that try to move from association to cause
senses.definitionCN: 统计与流行病学中描述从关联走向原因的方法
senses.example: The trial was designed for causal inference, not mere description.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验是为因果推断而设计，而不只是描述。
senses.why: The adjective now qualifies a method rather than a link. Causal inference is the disciplined attempt to earn the arrow that correlation alone cannot give.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词现在修饰方法，而不是连接。因果推断是有纪律的尝试，去赢得单靠相关无法给出的那支箭头。

senses.title: A causal explanation
senses.definition: an account that explains an event by identifying what brought it about
senses.definitionCN: 通过确认是什么造成了某事件来解释它的说法
senses.example: A causal explanation must rule out reverse causation.
senses.exampleCN: 因果解释必须排除反向因果。
senses.why: Explanation is the human activity, and causal marks its type. The word tells the reader that reasons of the 'because it produced' kind are coming, not reasons of purpose or meaning.
senses.whyCN: 解释是人的活动，causal 标示它的类型。这个词告诉读者，接下来的是“因为它造成了”这一类理由，而不是目的或意义类的理由。

senses.title: A causal chain
senses.definition: a sequence of events in which each link produces the next
senses.definitionCN: 每个环节都产生下一环节的一连串事件
senses.example: The causal chain from drought to conflict is long and indirect.
senses.exampleCN: 从干旱到冲突的因果链漫长而间接。
senses.why: The adjective makes chain a technical object. Once causes are linked in series, the question becomes where to cut the chain for responsibility or analysis.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把 chain 变成技术对象。一旦原因被串成系列，问题就变成：为了责任或分析，应该在哪一环切断。

senses.title: A causal model
senses.definition: a formal representation of assumed causal relations among variables
senses.definitionCN: 对变量之间假定因果关系的形式化表示
senses.example: The diagram is a causal model with arrows for assumed effects.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图是一个因果模型，用箭头表示假定的效应。
senses.why: Computing and statistics turned the adjective into a modelling term. A causal model does not prove causation; it states a hypothesis about which arrows exist.
senses.whyCN: 计算机与统计学把这个形容词变成建模术语。因果模型并不证明因果，它陈述一个关于哪些箭头存在的假设。

senses.title: A causal agent
senses.definition: the thing that actively produces an effect, especially in medicine or biology
senses.definitionCN: 主动产生效果的事物，尤用于医学或生物学
senses.example: The causal agent of the disease was a previously unknown virus.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病的致因体是一种此前未知的病毒。
senses.why: Here the adjective points to a concrete producer, not to a relation. A causal agent is the thing at the tail of the arrow, the one doing the producing.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词指向具体的产生者，而不是关系。致因主体是箭头尾端那个真正在起作用的东西。

senses.title: A causal factor in medicine
senses.definition: a condition that contributes to the development of a disease or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 促成某种疾病或结果发展的条件
senses.example: Air pollution is a causal factor in childhood asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 空气污染是儿童哮喘的一个致因因素。
senses.why: Medicine prefers this phrase because it allows several contributors at once. The adjective marks contribution to an outcome without claiming that one factor is solely responsible.
senses.whyCN: 医学偏爱这个说法，因为它允许同时有多个贡献者。这个形容词标示对结果的贡献，而不宣称某个因素是唯一责任者。

intro.en: Causal is the direct Latin adjective of causa, unlike causation, which came through the legal noun causatio. Its history is mostly the history of how philosophers and statisticians learned to qualify the word 'link'.
intro.cn: causal 是 causa 的直接拉丁形容词，与经法律名词 causatio 而来的 causation 不同。它的历史，主要是哲学家与统计学家学会如何修饰“连接”这个词的历史。

items.en: Causa meant 'cause, reason, motive' and also 'a legal case'. Every member of the English causal family goes back to this noun, including cause itself.
items.cn: causa 意为“原因、理由、动机”，也指“法律案件”。英语因果词族的每个成员，包括 cause 本身，都上溯到这个名词。

items.en: Causalis was formed with -alis, 'belonging to', and meant 'of a cause'. It was a learned adjective used in philosophy and grammar, not a word of ordinary Roman speech.
items.cn: causalis 由 -alis“属于……的”构成，意为“原因的”。它是哲学与语法中的学术形容词，不是罗马日常口语词。

items.en: English causal enters in the 16th century as the adjective corresponding to cause. Early uses are philosophical and grammatical, matching its Latin career.
items.cn: 英语 causal 在 16 世纪作为 cause 的对应形容词进入。早期用法属哲学与语法，与它的拉丁经历一致。

items.en: The phrase causal relation becomes central in debates over whether causes are observed or inferred. The adjective now modifies relation, connection and necessity, not only cause itself.
items.cn: causal relation 这一说法在“原因是被观察还是被推断”的争论中变得核心。这个形容词现在修饰 relation、connection、necessity，而不只是 cause 本身。

items.en: Medicine speaks of causal agents, and statistics of causal inference. Each field attaches the adjective to its own object: a pathogen, a variable, a mechanism.
items.cn: 医学谈致因主体，统计学谈因果推断。每个领域都把这个形容词接到自己的对象上：病原体、变量、机制。

items.en: Causal model, causal chain and causal factor are now standard across disciplines. The word has become the general adjective for any claim that one thing produces another.
items.cn: 因果模型、因果链、致因因素如今在各学科中都是标准说法。这个词已成为任何“一物产生另一物”之主张的通用形容词。

note.en: Causal is most often confused with casual, which looks and sounds close but has a completely different root. The first group makes that separation, then distinguishes the family members by part of speech.
note.cn: causal 最常与 casual 混淆，后者形音都近，却词根完全不同。第一组先做这个区分，再按词性区分同族词。

entries.definition: relaxed, informal, or happening by chance. It comes from Latin casus 'a fall, an occurrence', not from causa.
entries.definitionCN: 随意的、非正式的，或偶然发生的。它来自拉丁语 casus“落下、发生”，不是 causa。

entries.definition: actively producing an effect, or marking a cause in grammar. It is stronger than causal: it says something does cause, not merely relates to cause.
entries.definitionCN: 主动产生效果的，或在语法中标记使役的。它比 causal 更强：它说某物确实造成，而不只是与原因有关。

entries.definition: the cause-effect relation itself. Causal is the adjective; causation is the relation it describes.
entries.definitionCN: 因果关系本身。causal 是形容词，causation 是它所描述的关系。

entries.definition: relating to the causes of a disease. It is the medical specialist's word for what causal covers more broadly.
entries.definitionCN: 与疾病原因有关的。它是医学专家用来表达 causal 更宽含义的词。

entries.definition: describing a study of association without claimed causation. It is the deliberate opposite of causal in research design.
entries.definitionCN: 描述只研究关联而不主张因果的研究。在研究设计中，它是 causal 的刻意对立面。

entries.definition: serving to explain. It is broader than causal: an explanation can be functional or historical, not only causal.
entries.definitionCN: 用于解释的。它比 causal 更宽：解释可以是功能性的或历史性的，不只限于因果。

entries.definition: holding that events follow necessarily from prior conditions. It is a much stronger claim than causal.
entries.definitionCN: 主张事件必然由先前条件决定的。它比 causal 的主张强得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks separate causal from casual at the level of the root, then attach the adjective to six standard nouns it modifies.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩在词根层面把 causal 与 casual 分开，再把形容词接到它常修饰的六个标准名词上。

normal.en: Spell it with cause inside: c-a-u-s-a-l. The u comes from causa; casual has no u.
normal.cn: 记住里面藏着 cause：c-a-u-s-a-l。u 来自 causa；casual 没有 u。

normal.en: Pair the arrow: causal link is the arrow between two boxes.
normal.cn: 配箭头：causal link 是两个方框之间的箭头。

normal.en: Keep causal for relation, causative for producing.
normal.cn: causal 用于关系，causative 用于产生。

normal.en: In grammar, causal conjunctions give reasons: because, since, as.
normal.cn: 语法中表示原因的连词给理由：because、since、as。

normal.en: In statistics, causal inference tries to earn the arrow.
normal.cn: 统计中，因果推断试图赢得那支箭头。

abstract.en: Hold one arrow and one label: the arrow is causation, the label on it is causal.
abstract.cn: 抓住一支箭头和一个标签：箭头是 causation，贴在上面的标签是 causal。

abstract.en: Sort by the noun it modifies: link, relation, inference, mechanism, model, agent, factor, clause.
abstract.cn: 按所修饰的名词分组：联系、关系、推断、机制、模型、主体、因素、从句。

abstract.en: Remember the false friend: casual means relaxed or accidental, never causal.
abstract.cn: 记住假朋友：casual 意为随意或偶然，绝不是 causal。

examples.en: The evidence does not prove a causal relationship.
examples.cn: 这些证据不能证明因果关系。

examples.en: Because introduces a causal clause.
examples.cn: because 引出原因状语从句。

examples.en: Researchers use causal models to test competing explanations.
examples.cn: 研究者用因果模型来检验相互竞争的解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“考走”：把原因“考”察清楚才“走”下一步——causal 就是因果的。注意别和 casual“随意”混。

root: 拉丁语 causa“原因、理由、诉讼案件”加形容词后缀 -alis，构成晚期拉丁语 causalis“原因的”；英语 16 世纪直接借入作 causal。注意与 casus“落下、偶然”派生的 casual 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Causal is the adjective that marks an arrow. It can sit on the relation itself (causal link), on the method that tries to establish it (causal inference), on the thing that produces it (causal agent), or on the clause that states a reason (causal conjunction). The word never says the arrow is proven; it only says the claim is about cause.
sensesIntro.cn: causal 是给箭头贴标签的形容词。它可以贴在关系本身（causal link）、贴在试图确立关系的方法（causal inference）、贴在产生结果的事物（causal agent），或贴在陈述理由的从句（causal conjunction）。这个词从不宣称箭头已被证明，它只说这个主张是关于原因的。

core.en: The label on a cause-effect arrow: relating to who or what produces what.
core.cn: 贴在因果箭头上的标签：关于谁或什么产生了什么。

branches.en: THE LINK: general causal language, causal links, and whole chains.
branches.cn: 连接：一般因果语言、因果联系与整条链。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: clauses and conjunctions that state a reason.
branches.cn: 语法：陈述理由的从句与连词。

branches.en: METHOD: causal inference and formal causal models.
branches.cn: 方法：因果推断与形式化因果模型。

branches.en: EXPLANATION: an account organised around production.
branches.cn: 解释：围绕“产生”组织起来的说明。

branches.en: THE PRODUCER: agents and factors that contribute to an outcome.
branches.cn: 产生者：促成结果的主体与因素。

intro.en: Causal takes the Latin adjective suffix -alis, and its family spreads across -ity, -ly, -tion and -ative. The list shows the same base producing a noun of principle, a noun of relation, and an adverb.
intro.cn: causal 接拉丁形容词后缀 -alis，其词族分布在 -ity、-ly、-tion、-ative 上。清单展示同一词基如何生出原理名词、关系名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the noun of cause, its learned adjective, and the abstract noun of causality formed in later Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“原因”名词、其学术形容词，以及晚期拉丁语中构成的“因果性”抽象名词。

items.exampleCN: 他们没有发现因果联系。

items.meaning: the principle of cause and effect
items.example: The novel plays with ideas of causality.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说玩弄因果观念。

items.example: Causation is not established by correlation.
The suffix forms a causative verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成使役动词。

items.meaning: a connection held to produce an effect
items.example: The study reports a causal link.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究报告了一项因果联系。

items.meaning: reasoning from data to a causal claim
a clause that states a reason
items.example: The sentence begins with a causal clause.
items.exampleCN: 这个句子以原因状语从句开头。

items.meaning: a condition that contributes to an outcome
items.example: Stress is one causal factor in the illness.
items.exampleCN: 压力是这种疾病的一个致因因素。

definition_zh: 热带草原；（带散生乔木的）稀树草原；萨瓦纳
definition_en: tropical or subtropical grassland with scattered trees and a marked dry season
core_image: 旱季末尾，金黄的草海上零星立着几棵伞形金合欢，树影很短
scene: 旱季将尽，草海变成金黄色，零星的金合欢撑着伞形树冠立在其间。 In this savanna scattered acacias stand above a sea of grass that turns gold by the end of the dry season.
sceneCN: 这里 savanna 指「有旱季、散生乔木的热带草原」（第 1 个义项：稀树草原）；句意为在这片稀树草原上，零星金合欢立在旱季末尾变金的草海之上。图中可辨识物件：伞形树冠、金黄草层、短树影、远处灰白天空。

pos.zh: 稀树草原；热带草原（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 稀树草原化（森林退为稀树草原）

senses.title: Tropical grass with scattered trees
senses.definition: a tropical formation in which a continuous grass layer carries scattered trees, with a pronounced dry season
senses.definitionCN: 连续的草层上散布乔木、并有明显旱季的热带植被类型
senses.example: In this savanna scattered acacias stand above a sea of grass that turns gold by the end of the dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 在这片稀树草原上，零星金合欢立在旱季末尾变金的草海之上。
senses.why: the word names a mixture, not a pure type: grass is continuous, trees are present but never close a canopy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一种混合，而非纯型：草层连续，树虽有却从不闭合树冠。

senses.title: A climate with a long dry season
senses.titleCN: 有明显旱季的草原气候
senses.definition: the tropical climate type with a wet season and a long dry season, classified Aw in Koppen's scheme
senses.definitionCN: 有雨季与长旱季的热带气候型，在柯本分类中属热带干湿季气候
senses.example: The savanna climate gives eight dry months and four wet ones.
senses.exampleCN: 稀树草原气候给出八个月旱季与四个月雨季。
senses.why: the vegetation type gave its name to the climate that produces it, since the dry season is what keeps trees apart.
senses.whyCN: 植被类型为造成它的气候命名，因为正是旱季让树彼此分开。

senses.title: Savanna woodland structure
senses.definition: a savanna in which trees are dense enough to form a broken canopy over the grass
senses.definitionCN: 树木密到能在草层上方形成断续树冠的稀树草原
senses.example: Savanna woodland shades out the tallest grasses beneath it.
senses.exampleCN: 稀树草原林地把下方最高的草遮死。
senses.why: adding woodland marks the upper end of tree density, where the mixture begins to look like open forest.
senses.whyCN: 加上「疏林」标出树木密度的上端，此时混合已开始像疏林。

senses.title: Habitat for large grazers
senses.definition: the grass-and-tree mosaic that supports herds, their predators and seasonal migration
senses.definitionCN: 支撑兽群、捕食者与季节性迁徙的草树镶嵌体
senses.example: The savanna feeds the largest land migration on Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 这片稀树草原供养着地球上规模最大的陆地迁徙。
senses.why: the mixture offers grass for grazers and cover for hunters, so the type becomes shorthand for a whole fauna.
senses.whyCN: 混合结构为食草者提供草、为猎手提供隐蔽，于是这一类型成了一整套动物群的代称。

senses.title: A fire-maintained landscape
senses.definition: a savanna whose open structure persists only because repeated fires kill young trees
senses.definitionCN: 只有反复火烧杀死幼树，其开阔结构才得以维持的稀树草原
senses.example: Without savanna fire, the grass would close into thicket.
senses.exampleCN: 没有稀树草原火，草地将闭合成灌丛。
senses.why: fire is not a disturbance here but a maintenance tool, which is why the type is described as fire-dependent.
senses.whyCN: 在此火不是干扰而是维护手段，因此该类型被称为依赖火。

senses.title: Derived savanna from cleared forest
senses.titleCN: 由森林清除形成的次生稀树草原
senses.definition: grass-and-tree land produced by clearing or repeated burning of former forest
senses.definitionCN: 由清除或反复焚烧原森林而形成的草树混合地
senses.example: Much of the derived savanna was forest two generations ago.
senses.exampleCN: 大片次生稀树草原在两代人以前还是森林。
senses.why: the same cover can be ancient or recent, and 'derived' marks the human-made version.
senses.whyCN: 同样的覆盖既可能是古老的，也可能是新近的，「派生」一词标出人为形成的那一种。

senses.title: The ancient spread of C4 grassland
senses.titleCN: 古生态中四碳草地的扩张
senses.definition: the Miocene expansion of tropical grass biomes as C4 grasses and seasonal rainfall spread
senses.definitionCN: 随四碳草类与季节性降水扩张而发生的中新世热带草地扩展
senses.example: The savanna expanded as C4 grasses spread across the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 随着四碳草类在热带扩散，稀树草原也扩张。
senses.why: palaeoecology uses the modern cover word for a deep-time event, because the same structure can be read from fossils.
senses.whyCN: 古生态学用现代覆盖词指深时事件，因为同样的结构可从化石中读出。

senses.title: The savannah spelling variant
senses.definition: an alternative spelling with a doubled n, common in place names and in older British writing
senses.definitionCN: 双写 n 的异体拼写，常见于地名与较早的英式书写
senses.example: Older maps print savannah where modern surveys write savanna.
senses.exampleCN: 旧地图印作 savannah，现代调查写作 savanna。
senses.why: the doubled form reflects an earlier attempt to render the Spanish source; both spellings name the same cover.
senses.whyCN: 双写形式反映早期对西班牙语来源的转写尝试；两种拼写都指同一种覆盖。

intro.en: Savanna is a New World loan, probably from a Carib or Taino word for open grass, carried into English through Spanish sabana.
intro.cn: savanna 是新大陆借词，很可能出自加勒比或泰诺语表示开阔草地的词，经西班牙语 sabana 进入英语。

items.en: The source is usually given as a Carib or Taino word meaning 'open grassland' or 'plain'. The exact form and language are not settled.
items.cn: 来源通常被说成加勒比语或泰诺语中表示「开阔草地、平原」的词。确切形式与语种并无定论。

items.en: Spanish sabana recorded the word in the sixteenth century and passed it to other European languages.
items.cn: 西班牙语 sabana 在 16 世纪记录了这个词，并把它传给其他欧洲语言。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, first describing Caribbean and South American plains.
items.cn: 英语在 16 至 17 世纪借入，最初描述加勒比与南美的平原。

items.en: Colonial writers later applied the American word to African grass-and-tree country, and that usage now dominates.
items.cn: 殖民时期的作者后来把这个美洲词用在非洲的草树地带，这一用法如今占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (language and first date): the Carib/Taino origin is a common attribution rather than a documented derivation, and the first English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（语种与首见年代）：加勒比/泰诺来源属常见归属，并非有文献证明的派生；最早英语书证年代亦不可靠。

note.en: Group one gathers the regional grass-and-tree names often used interchangeably; group two gathers the general cover words around them.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的各地草树地带名称；第二组是周边通用的覆盖词。

entries.definition: The doubled-n spelling of the same word, frequent in place names such as Savannah, Georgia.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的双写 n 拼法，常见于地名，如佐治亚州的萨凡纳。

entries.definition: North American temperate grassland with essentially no trees, unlike savanna.
entries.definitionCN: 北美温带草原，基本无树，与稀树草原不同。

entries.definition: Eurasian short-grass plain with cold winters; it lacks the tropical dry season of savanna.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季寒冷的欧亚短草平原；没有稀树草原的热带旱季。

entries.definition: Southern African open grassland; some types approach savanna but the term is regional.
entries.definitionCN: 南部非洲开阔草地；某些类型接近稀树草原，但该词是地区性的。

entries.definition: Any grass-dominated land; savanna is the tropical, tree-dotted member of the class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何以草为主的土地；savanna 是该类中热带、带散生树的成员。

entries.definition: Southern African savanna with abundant shrubs; it stresses the woody component.
entries.definitionCN: 灌木丰富的南部非洲稀树草原；强调木本成分。

entries.definition: The seasonally flooded plains of the Orinoco basin; a regional savanna type.
entries.definitionCN: 奥里诺科河流域季节性泛滥的平原；一种地区性稀树草原。

entries.definition: Brazilian tropical savanna with twisted trees and deep roots; a regional type with its own flora.
entries.definitionCN: 巴西热带稀树草原，树形扭曲、根深；有独特植物区系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Grass continuous, trees scattered, dry season long: that is the savanna formula.
normal.cn: 草层连续、树木散布、旱季漫长：这就是稀树草原的公式。

normal.en: The route is Carib/Taino → Spanish sabana → English savanna.
normal.cn: 路径是加勒比/泰诺语 → 西班牙语 sabana → 英语 savanna。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: savanna climate, savanna woodland, savanna fire.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：稀树草原气候、稀树草原林地、草原火。

normal.en: Regional cousins: llanos, cerrado, bushveld, veld.
normal.cn: 地区近亲：llanos、cerrado、bushveld、veld。

normal.en: The image is a gold grass sea with a few umbrella acacias.
normal.cn: 意象是金黄草海上立着几棵伞形金合欢。

abstract.en: Think of a lawn that keeps a few trees on purpose so animals have both food and shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一片故意留下几棵树的草地，让动物既有食物又有荫。

abstract.en: Think of a balance held in place by fire, not by climate alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一种平衡靠火而非仅靠气候维持。

abstract.en: Think of a word borrowed from one continent and then rented out to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从一块大陆借来、又转租给另一块大陆的词。

examples.en: Elephants push over savanna trees to reach the grass below.
examples.cn: 大象推倒稀树草原上的树，以吃到下面的草。

examples.en: Savanna fires recycle nutrients faster than decomposition can.
examples.cn: 稀树草原火循环养分的速度快于分解。

examples.en: The boundary between forest and savanna shifts with rainfall.
examples.cn: 森林与稀树草原的边界随降水移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「savanna」谐音「沙凡纳」——沙地上稀疏长着伞形树的草原 → 稀树草原

root: 可能出自加勒比语或泰诺语表示「开阔草地」的词 → 西班牙语 sabana → 英语 savanna。确切语种与形式不确定，属常见归属而非有文献证明的派生。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses read the same mixture as vegetation, climate, woodland, habitat, fire regime, derived land, fossil record and spelling variant.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种混合分别读成植被、气候、林地、生境、火情制度、次生地、化石记录与拼写变体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold sea of grass with a few umbrella-shaped trees above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：金黄的草海之上立着几棵伞形树。

branches.en: MIXTURE: continuous grass and scattered trees, produced by a long dry season.
branches.cn: 混合：连续草层与散生树，由漫长旱季造成。

branches.en: DENSITY: as trees thicken, the same cover approaches woodland.
branches.cn: 密度：树变密时，同一覆盖接近疏林。

branches.en: FAUNA AND FIRE: grass feeds herds, cover hides hunters, and fire keeps the trees young.
branches.cn: 动物与火：草养兽群，树提供隐蔽，火让树保持幼态。

branches.en: TIME: the cover can be made by clearing or read back into the Miocene fossil record.
branches.cn: 时间：这种覆盖可由清林造成，也可回读至中新世化石记录。

branches.en: SPELLING: a doubled n marks the older transcription, not a different landscape.
branches.cn: 拼写：双写 n 只标出较早的转写，并非另一种景观。

intro.en: Savanna is a borrowed simplex with no productive affixes of its own; its family is made of compounds and regional names.
intro.cn: savanna 是借来的单纯词，本身不带能产后缀；其词族由复合词与地区名构成。

latinIntro.en: The immediate source is Spanish, but the word's deeper origin is American, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是西班牙语，但更深来源属美洲语言，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The savanna stretched to the river.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原一直伸到河边。

items.meaning: savanna with a broken tree canopy
items.meaningCN: 有断续树冠的稀树草原
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原林地沿河分布。

items.example: The savanna climate suits drought-hardy crops.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原气候适合耐旱作物。
反复焚烧之后出现稀树草原化。

items.meaning: the grass-tree system as a whole
items.example: The savanna ecosystem depends on seasonal rain.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原生态系统依赖季节性降水。

items.example: Dry savanna grades into thorn scrub.
items.exampleCN: 干旱稀树草原逐渐过渡为刺灌丛。
